title.zh: 卷二百四十 列傳第一百二十八 葉向高 劉一燝 韓爌 朱國祚 何宗彥 孫如游
title.en: Volume 240 Biographies 128: Ye Xianggao, Liu Yijing, Han Kuang, Zhu Guozuo, He Zongyan, Sun Ruyou
title.raw: 卷二百四十 列傳第一百二十八 葉向高 劉一燝 韓爌 朱國祚 何宗彥 孫如游 Volume 240 Biographies 128: Ye Xianggao, Liu Yijing, Han Kuang, Zhu Guozuo, He Zongyan, Sun Ruyou

sentences.zh: 葉向高

translations.literal: Ye Xianggao
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao

sentences.zh: 葉向高，字進卿，福清人。

translations.literal: Ye Xianggao, styled Jinqing, was a native of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao, courtesy name Jinqing, came from Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 父朝榮，養利知州。

translations.literal: His father Chaorong was prefect of Yangli.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ye Chaorong had served as prefect of Yangli.

sentences.zh: 向高甫妊，母避倭難，生道旁敗廁中。

translations.literal: When Xianggao was still in the womb, his mother fled the Japanese raids and gave birth to him in a ruined privy by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: While his mother was still carrying him, she fled the Japanese raids and bore him in a ruined roadside latrine.

sentences.zh: 數瀕死，輒有神相之。

translations.literal: He nearly died many times, yet each time some divine power seemed to protect him.
translations.idiomatic: He came close to death again and again, yet each time seemed to be spared by some providential hand.

sentences.zh: 舉萬曆十一年進士，授庶吉士，進編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Wanli, was appointed a Hanlin bachelor, and was promoted to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Wanli 11 (1583), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and rose to compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷南京國子司業，改左中允，仍視司業事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be vice director of the Nanjing Directorate of Education, then changed to left junior mentor while still overseeing the vice director's duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Nanjing as vice director of the Directorate of Education, then made left junior mentor while continuing to handle the vice director's work.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，召為左庶子，充皇長子侍班官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was summoned as left senior mentor and appointed attendant on the heir apparent's study sessions.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 26 (1598) he was recalled to serve as left senior mentor and attendant at the crown prince's lectures.

sentences.zh: 礦稅橫行，向高上班，引東漢西邸聚錢事為鑒，不報。

translations.literal: As mining levies ran rampant, Xianggao submitted a memorial to court, citing the Eastern Han precedent of the Western Residence amassing money as a warning; he received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: With mining taxes running unchecked, he memorialized the throne, citing how the Eastern Han Western Residence had hoarded wealth as a cautionary example; the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 尋擢南京禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to right vice minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right vice minister of Rites in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，改吏部。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 再陳礦稅之害，又請罷遼東稅監高淮，語皆切至。

translations.literal: He again set forth the harm of mining levies and also asked that Gao Huai, the tax superintendent in Liaodong, be removed; his language was altogether trenchant.
translations.idiomatic: He again laid out the damage done by mining levies and called for the dismissal of Gao Huai, the Liaodong tax superintendent; his words were blunt and forceful.

sentences.zh: 妖書獄興，移書沈一貫力諫。

translations.literal: When the seditionous-book case arose, he wrote to Shen Yiguan urging him strongly to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: When the seditionous-book affair broke, he wrote to Shen Yiguan urging him to protest vigorously.

sentences.zh: 一貫不悅，以故滯南京九年。

translations.literal: Yiguan was displeased, and for this reason Xianggao remained stuck in Nanjing for nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan took offense, and for that reason Xianggao languished in Nanjing for nine years.

sentences.zh: 後一貫罷，沈鯉亦去，朱賡獨當國。

translations.literal: Later Yiguan was dismissed, Shen Li also left office, and Zhu Geng alone directed the government.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Yiguan was removed and Shen Li had also left, Zhu Geng alone ran the government.

sentences.zh: 帝命增閣臣。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that Grand Secretaries be added.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered additional Grand Secretaries appointed.

sentences.zh: 三十五年五月，擢向高禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，與王錫爵、于慎行、李廷機並命。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirty-fifth year Xianggao was promoted to minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, appointed together with Wang Xijue, Yu Shenxing, and Li Tingji.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Wanli 35 (1607) he was made minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, along with Wang Xijue, Yu Shenxing, and Li Tingji.

sentences.zh: 十一月，向高入朝，慎行已先卒，錫爵堅辭不出。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xianggao entered court; Shenxing had already died beforehand, and Xijue firmly declined to take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xianggao came to court; Shenxing had already died, and Xijue steadfastly refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 明年，首輔賡亦卒，次輔廷機以人言久杜門，向高遂獨相。

translations.literal: The next year the chief minister Geng also died; the second minister Tingji had long shut his doors on account of public talk, and Xianggao thus became sole chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chief Minister Zhu Geng also died; Second Minister Li Tingji had long stayed home amid public criticism, and Xianggao became the sole chief minister.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝在位日久，倦勤，朝事多廢弛，大僚或空署，士大夫推擇遷轉之命往往不下，上下乖隔甚。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had been on the throne a long while, was weary of diligence, and court affairs were largely neglected; high offices were sometimes left vacant, and orders for the promotion and transfer of scholar-officials often were not issued; estrangement between above and below was very great.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had reigned so long that he had grown weary of governing; court business languished, senior posts often stood empty, and appointments for scholar-officials frequently never issued—the court and the throne had grown far apart.

sentences.zh: 廷臣部黨勢漸成，而中官榷稅、開礦，大為民害。

translations.literal: Factional cliques among court officials gradually took shape, while eunuchs imposed transit levies and opened mines, greatly harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: Court factions were taking shape among the officials, while eunuchs levied transit taxes and opened mines to the people's great harm.

sentences.zh: 帝又寵鄭貴妃，福王不肯之國。

translations.literal: The emperor also favored Consort Zheng, and the Prince of Fu would not go to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also favored Consort Zheng, and the Prince of Fu refused to leave for his assigned domain.

sentences.zh: 向高用宿望居相位，憂國奉公，每事執爭效忠藎。

translations.literal: Xianggao, by virtue of long-standing prestige, held the chief ministership; he grieved for the state and served the public good, disputing every matter and striving with loyal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao held the chief ministership on the strength of his long-standing reputation; grieving for the realm and serving the public interest, he contested issue after issue with loyal zeal.

sentences.zh: 帝心重向高，體貌優厚，然其言大抵格不用，所救正十二三而已。

translations.literal: In his heart the emperor valued Xianggao and treated him with generous regard, yet his words were for the most part blocked and not adopted; only one or two out of ten of his corrections were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held Xianggao in esteem and treated him generously, yet most of his advice was set aside; only a tenth or so of what he tried to set right was accepted.

sentences.zh: 東宮輟講者五年，廷臣屢請不得命。

translations.literal: Lectures for the Eastern Palace had been suspended for five years; court officials repeatedly petitioned but received no order.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction for the crown prince had been suspended for five years, and repeated petitions from the court brought no response.

sentences.zh: 三十七年二月，向高擇吉以請，亦不報。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-seventh year Xianggao chose an auspicious day to petition; again there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wanli 37 (1609) Xianggao chose an auspicious day to petition again; still there was no answer.

sentences.zh: 自是歲春秋必懇請，帝皆不納。

translations.literal: From then on each spring and autumn he earnestly petitioned, but the emperor accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he pleaded earnestly every spring and autumn, but the emperor would not consent.

sentences.zh: 貴妃王氏，太子生母也，薨四日不發喪。

translations.literal: Consort Wang, the crown prince's birth mother, died, yet for four days no mourning was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang, the crown prince's own mother, had died, yet four days passed with no mourning proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 向高以為言，乃發喪。

translations.literal: Xianggao spoke on the matter, and only then was mourning proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Xianggao spoke up was mourning finally ordered.

sentences.zh: 而禮官上其儀註，稽五日不行。

translations.literal: Yet when the ritual officials submitted the prescribed observances, they were held up for five days without implementation.
translations.idiomatic: When the ritual officials submitted the prescribed rites, they sat for five days without approval.

sentences.zh: 向高復爭之，疏乃下。

translations.literal: Xianggao again contested it, and only then was the memorial issued.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao protested again, and only then was the order issued.

sentences.zh: 福王府第成，工部以之國請，向高擬旨上。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu's mansion was completed, the Ministry of Works petitioned that he go to his fief; Xianggao drafted the rescript and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu's residence was finished, the Ministry of Works petitioned for his departure to his fief; Xianggao drafted the rescript and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 帝不發，改明春。

translations.literal: The emperor did not issue it and changed the date to the coming spring.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withheld it and postponed departure until the following spring.

sentences.zh: 及期迫，向高請先飭儀衛舟車，帝不納。

translations.literal: When the deadline drew near, Xianggao asked that the guard of honor and boats and carriages be prepared in advance; the emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: As the deadline approached, Xianggao asked that escorts, boats, and carriages be prepared in advance; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 四十一年春，廷臣交章請，復諭改明春。

translations.literal: In the spring of the forty-first year court officials submitted memorial after memorial requesting departure, and again an edict postponed it to the coming spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Wanli 41 (1613) officials submitted memorial after memorial, and again the court was told to wait until the following spring.

sentences.zh: 已，忽傳旨，莊田非四萬頃不行，廷臣大駭。

translations.literal: Then suddenly an edict was transmitted: unless estate lands amounted to forty thousand qing he would not go; court officials were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Then suddenly came word that he would not leave unless his estate lands totaled forty thousand qing; the court was appalled.

sentences.zh: 向高因進曰：「田四萬頃，必不能足，之國且無日，明旨又不信於天下矣。

translations.literal: Xianggao thereupon advanced and said: "Forty thousand qing of land certainly cannot be made complete; the day of going to the fief is still nowhere in sight, and the clear edict will no longer be trusted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao stepped forward and said: "Forty thousand qing can never be supplied; his departure has no date in sight, and the throne's clear word will no longer be believed under heaven.

sentences.zh: 且王疏引祖制，而祖制無有是事。

translations.literal: Moreover, in his memorial the prince cited ancestral institutions, yet ancestral institutions contain no such matter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the prince's memorial cites ancestral precedent, yet no such precedent exists.

sentences.zh: 曩惟世宗時景王有之。

translations.literal: In the past only under Emperor Shizong did the Prince of Jing have it.
translations.idiomatic: In the past only the Prince of Jing under Emperor Shizong had such a case.

sentences.zh: 景王久不之國，皇考在裕邸，危疑不安，此何可效也？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing long did not go to his fief; the present emperor's father was at the Residence of Plenty in peril and uncertainty—how can this be imitated?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jing long delayed his departure; your father's own father lived at the Residence of Plenty in fear and uncertainty—how can we follow that example?

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「莊田自有成例，且今大分已定，何猜？」

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "Estate lands have their own established precedents, and moreover the great allotment is now settled—why suspicion?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Estate lands follow established precedent, and the succession is settled—why suspect anything?"

sentences.zh: 向高因疏謝，言：「皇考時，名位雖未正，然講讀不輟，情意通。

translations.literal: Xianggao thereupon submitted a memorial of thanks, saying: "In the time of your father's father, though title and position were not yet settled, lectures and study did not cease, and feelings were in communication.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao submitted a follow-up memorial, saying: "In your father's day, though his status was not yet secure, lectures never stopped and the bond between father and son remained open.

sentences.zh: 今東宮輟講八年，且不奉天顏久，而福王一日兩見，以故不能無疑。

translations.literal: Now the Eastern Palace has suspended lectures for eight years, and has long not beheld the imperial countenance, while the Prince of Fu is granted audience twice in one day—for this reason suspicion cannot be absent.
translations.idiomatic: Now the crown prince has gone eight years without instruction and long without seeing your face, while the Prince of Fu is received twice in a single day—how can there be no suspicion?

sentences.zh: 惟堅守明春期，而無以莊田藉口，天下疑自釋。」

translations.literal: Only by firmly holding to the coming spring deadline and not using estate lands as a pretext will suspicion throughout the realm release itself."
translations.idiomatic: Hold firm to next spring's deadline and give no pretext over estate lands, and suspicion under heaven will lift of itself."

sentences.zh: 帝報福王無一日兩見事。

translations.literal: The emperor replied that the Prince of Fu had no matter of two audiences in one day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that the Prince of Fu was not received twice in one day.

sentences.zh: 向高有裁斷，善處大事。

translations.literal: Xianggao had decisive judgment and was skilled at handling great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao was decisive and adept at handling crises.

sentences.zh: 錦衣百戶王曰乾者，京師奸人也，與孔學、趙宗舜、趙思聖等相訐告。

translations.literal: Wang Rigian, a hundred-household officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was a villain of the capital who mutually accused Kong Xue, Zhao Zongshun, Zhao Sisheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rigian, a hundred-household officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was a scoundrel of the capital who had been trading accusations with Kong Xue, Zhao Zongshun, Zhao Sisheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 刑官讞未竟，曰乾乃入皇城放炮上疏。

translations.literal: Before the judicial officials had finished their verdict, Rigian entered the Imperial City, fired cannon, and submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Before the judges had finished their inquiry, Rigian entered the Imperial City, fired cannon, and submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 刑官大驚，將擬曰乾死罪。

translations.literal: The judicial officials were greatly alarmed and were about to sentence Rigian to death.
translations.idiomatic: The judges were alarmed and were about to sentence Rigian to death.

sentences.zh: 曰乾遂訐奏鄭妃內侍姜嚴山與學等及妖人王三詔用厭勝術詛咒皇太后、皇太子死，擁立福王。

translations.literal: Rigian then accused in a memorial that the palace attendant of Consort Zheng, Jiang Yanshan, together with Xue and others and the sorcerer Wang Sanzhao, used witchcraft to curse the empress dowager and crown prince to death and install the Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Rigian then accused Consort Zheng's attendant Jiang Yanshan, Kong Xue and his associates, and the sorcerer Wang Sanzhao of using witchcraft to curse the empress dowager and crown prince to death and install the Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，繞殿行半日，曰：「此大變事，宰相何無言？」

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken with rage, paced around the hall for half a day, and said: "This is a matter of great upheaval—why is the chief minister silent?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, paced the hall for half a day, and cried: "This is a calamity—why has the chief minister said nothing?

sentences.zh: 內侍即跪上向高奏。

translations.literal: A palace attendant immediately knelt and presented Xianggao's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch at once knelt and presented Xianggao's memorial.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「此事大類往年妖書，然妖書匿名難詰，今兩造具在，一訊即情得。

translations.literal: The memorial said: "This affair greatly resembles the seditionous-book case of years past, yet that case was anonymous and hard to investigate; now both parties are present, and one interrogation will bring out the facts.
translations.idiomatic: It read: "This resembles the seditionous-book affair of years past, but that case was anonymous and hard to pursue; here both sides are at hand, and one interrogation will settle the truth.

sentences.zh: 陛下當靜處之，稍張皇，則中外大擾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should handle it calmly; if you show the slightest alarm, court and country will be greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should handle this calmly; the slightest panic will throw the realm into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 至其詞牽引貴妃、福王，尤可痛恨。

translations.literal: As for its words implicating the honored consort and the Prince of Fu, they are especially detestable.
translations.idiomatic: As for dragging in the honored consort and the Prince of Fu, that is especially hateful.

sentences.zh: 臣與九卿所見皆同，敢以聞。」

translations.literal: Your servant and the nine ministers are all of one view and venture to inform Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant and the nine ministers share this view and venture to report it.

sentences.zh: 帝讀竟太息曰：「吾父子兄弟全矣。」

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished reading, he sighed deeply and said: "My father and son, my brothers, are all secure."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had finished reading, he sighed and said: "My father and son, my brothers—all are safe."

sentences.zh: 明日，向高又言：「曰乾疏不宜發。

translations.literal: The next day Xianggao again said: "Rigian's memorial should not be issued.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xianggao said again: "Rigian's memorial should not be circulated.

sentences.zh: 發則上驚聖母，下驚東宮，貴妃、福王皆不安。

translations.literal: If issued, above it will alarm the empress dowager, below it will alarm the Eastern Palace, and the honored consort and Prince of Fu will all be uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: If it is issued, it will alarm the empress dowager above and the crown prince below, and neither the honored consort nor the Prince of Fu will be at ease.

sentences.zh: 宜留中，而別諭法司治諸奸人罪，且速定明春之國期，以息群喙，則天下帖然無事。」

translations.literal: It should be kept within the palace, while separately instructing the judicial offices to punish the villains' crimes, and quickly fixing the coming spring date for going to the fief to quiet the many voices—then all under heaven will be settled and without incident."
translations.idiomatic: Keep it within the palace, separately instruct the judicial offices to punish the villains, and fix next spring's departure date at once to silence the clamor—then all under heaven will be calm."

sentences.zh: 帝盡用其言，太子、福王得相安。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted his words entirely; the crown prince and Prince of Fu were able to live in mutual peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice entirely, and the crown prince and Prince of Fu were able to coexist in peace.

sentences.zh: 貴妃終不欲福王之國，言明年冬太后七十壽，王宜留慶賀。

translations.literal: The honored consort ultimately did not wish the Prince of Fu to go to his fief, saying that the next winter the empress dowager would celebrate her seventieth birthday and the prince ought to remain to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The honored consort still did not want the Prince of Fu to leave, saying that the empress dowager's seventieth birthday fell the next winter and the prince should stay to celebrate.

sentences.zh: 帝令內閣宣諭。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Grand Secretariat to proclaim the instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Grand Secretariat to announce this.

sentences.zh: 向高留上諭弗宣，請今冬預行慶壽禮，如期之國。

translations.literal: Xianggao withheld the imperial instruction and did not proclaim it, asking instead to hold the birthday celebration this winter in advance and have the prince go to his fief on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao held back the imperial instruction and did not announce it, proposing instead to hold the birthday celebration early this winter and send the prince to his fief on schedule.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中使至向高私邸，必欲下前諭。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace messenger to Xianggao's private residence, insisting on issuing the earlier instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace messenger to Xianggao's home, insisting the earlier instruction be issued.

sentences.zh: 向高言：「外廷喧傳陛下欲假賀壽名留福王，約千人伏闕請。

translations.literal: Xianggao said: "Outside court it is loudly rumored that Your Majesty wishes to use the birthday celebration as a pretext to keep the Prince of Fu, with about a thousand men lying in wait at the palace gate to petition.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said: "Outside court it is widely rumored that Your Majesty means to use the birthday celebration as a pretext to keep the Prince of Fu, with a thousand men ready to petition at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 今果有此諭，人情益疑駴，將信王曰乾妖言，朝端必不靜。

translations.literal: If this instruction is now truly issued, popular feeling will grow more suspicious and alarmed; people will believe Wang Rigian's sorcerous talk, and the court will certainly not be tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: If this instruction is now issued, suspicion will only deepen; people will believe Rigian's sorcerous claims, and the court will not be calm.

sentences.zh: 聖母聞之，亦必不樂。

translations.literal: If the empress dowager hears of it, she too will certainly be displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, hearing of it, will surely be displeased as well.

sentences.zh: 且潞王聖母愛子，亦居外藩，何惓惓福王為？」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Lu, whom the empress dowager loves as a son, also dwells in an outer fief—why be so intent on the Prince of Fu?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Prince of Lu, whom she loves as a son, also lives in an outer fief—why be so set on keeping the Prince of Fu?

sentences.zh: 因封還手諭。

translations.literal: He thereupon sealed and returned the handwritten instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the handwritten instruction and returned it.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已從之，福王乃之國。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice but to comply, and the Prince of Fu then went to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to agree, and the Prince of Fu finally departed for his fief.

sentences.zh: 向高嘗上疏言：「今天下必亂必危之道，蓋有數端，而災傷寇盜物怪人妖不與焉。

translations.literal: Xianggao once submitted a memorial saying: "The ways by which the realm today will surely fall into disorder and peril are several in number, and natural disasters, banditry, strange things, and human portents are not among them.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao once memorialized: "The paths by which the realm will surely fall into chaos and danger are several, and natural disasters, bandits, strange omens, and sorcery are not among them.

sentences.zh: 廊廟空虛，一也。

translations.literal: The court halls stand empty—this is the first.
translations.idiomatic: The halls of state stand empty—that is the first.

sentences.zh: 上下否隔，二也。

translations.literal: Above and below are blocked off from each other—this is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Throne and officials are cut off from one another—that is the second.

sentences.zh: 士大夫好勝喜爭，三也。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials love victory and delight in strife—this is the third.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials love victory and relish strife—that is the third.

sentences.zh: 多藏厚積，必有悖出之釁，四也。

translations.literal: Those who hoard much and accumulate deeply will surely bring forth rebellious outbreaks—this is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hoard great wealth will surely breed violent upheaval—that is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 風聲氣習日趨日下，莫可挽回，五也。

translations.literal: Public reputation and moral habit daily decline further, beyond all recovery—this is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Public morals sink day by day beyond recall—that is the fifth.

sentences.zh: 非陛下奮然振作，簡任老成，布列朝署，取積年廢弛政事一舉新之，恐宗社之憂，不在敵國外患，而即在廟堂之上也。」

translations.literal: Unless Your Majesty rouses yourself vigorously, selects and appoints seasoned men, stations them throughout the court offices, and in one stroke renews years of neglected administration, I fear the worry for altars and state lies not with enemy states and external troubles but right within the temple hall itself.
translations.idiomatic: Unless Your Majesty rouses yourself, appoints seasoned men of experience throughout the court, and in one stroke renews years of neglected government, I fear the danger to the dynasty lies not with foreign enemies but within these very halls.

sentences.zh: 其言絕痛切。

translations.literal: His words were utterly painful and trenchant.
translations.idiomatic: His words were painfully blunt.

sentences.zh: 帝知其忠愛，不能行。

translations.literal: The emperor knew his loyal devotion but could not act on it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recognized his loyal devotion but could not act on it.

sentences.zh: 初，向高入閣。

translations.literal: When Xianggao first entered the Grand Secretariat,
translations.idiomatic: When Xianggao first entered the Grand Secretariat,

sentences.zh: 未幾，陳用人理財策，力請補缺官，罷礦稅。

translations.literal: before long he set forth policies on employing men and managing finances, strongly petitioning to fill vacant offices and abolish mining levies.
translations.idiomatic: he soon laid out policies on appointments and finances, urgently calling for vacant posts to be filled and mining levies abolished.

sentences.zh: 見帝不能從，乃陳上下乖離之病。

translations.literal: Seeing that the emperor could not follow, he then set forth the malady of estrangement between above and below.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the emperor would not comply, he set forth the malady of estrangement between throne and court.

sentences.zh: 兩疏乞罷，帝不允。

translations.literal: In two memorials he begged to resign; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He twice petitioned to resign; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 向高自獨相，即請增閣臣，帝不聽。

translations.literal: From the time Xianggao became sole chief minister he at once asked to add Grand Secretaries; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became sole chief minister, he at once asked for additional Grand Secretaries; the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 及吏部尚書孫丕揚以薦賢不用求去，向高特疏請留，亦不報，遂引疾。

translations.literal: When Sun Piyang, minister of Personnel, asked to leave because his recommendations of worthy men were not used, Xianggao specially memorialized asking that he be retained; again there was no reply, and he thereupon cited illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Piyang, minister of Personnel, asked to resign because his recommended candidates were not appointed, Xianggao specially memorialized to keep him; again there was no reply, and he cited illness.

sentences.zh: 屢諭，乃出視事。

translations.literal: After repeated edicts he then came out to attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated imperial messages he returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 已，又言：「臣屢求去，輒蒙恩諭留。

translations.literal: Later he again said: "Your servant has repeatedly asked to leave, yet each time received gracious edicts to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Later he said again: "Your servant has repeatedly asked to leave, yet each time been graciously told to stay.

sentences.zh: 顧臣不在一身去留，而在國家治亂。

translations.literal: Yet your servant's concern is not the going or staying of one person, but the order or disorder of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my concern is not whether one man stays or goes, but whether the state is governed or in chaos.

sentences.zh: 今天下所在災傷死亡，畿輔、中州、齊魯流移載道，加中外空虛，人才俱盡。

translations.literal: Today wherever one looks under heaven there are disasters, injuries, and deaths; in the capital region, the central provinces, and Qi and Lu, displaced people fill the roads; added to this, court and country are empty, and talent is altogether exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Today disasters and death afflict every region; in the capital district, the central provinces, and Qi and Lu the roads are crowded with refugees; court and country alike stand empty, and talent is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 罪不在他人，臣何可不去。

translations.literal: The fault lies not with others—how can your servant not leave?
translations.idiomatic: The fault is not others'—how can your servant not leave?"

sentences.zh: 且陛下用臣，則當行其言。

translations.literal: Moreover, if Your Majesty employs your servant, you ought to carry out his words.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if Your Majesty employs me, you ought to act on my words.

sentences.zh: 今章奏不發，大僚不補，起廢不行，臣微誠不能上達，留何益？

translations.literal: Now memorials are not issued, high offices are not filled, restoration of dismissed officials is not carried out—your servant's slight sincerity cannot reach above; what good is remaining?
translations.idiomatic: Now memorials go unanswered, senior posts unfilled, and dismissed officials unreinstated—my modest counsel cannot reach you; what good is my staying?

sentences.zh: 誠用臣言，不徒縻臣身，臣溘先朝露，有餘幸矣。」

translations.literal: If you truly use your servant's words, it will not merely tether his person; even if your servant expires before the morning dew, he would still have surplus fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly act on my counsel, it will not merely keep me in office; even if I die at once, I would count myself fortunate.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 京師大水，四方多奏水旱。

translations.literal: The capital suffered great floods; from all quarters many reports came of flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods struck the capital, and reports of flood and drought poured in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 向高又言：「自閣臣至九卿臺省，曹署皆空，南都九卿亦止存其二。

translations.literal: Xianggao again said: "From Grand Secretaries down to the nine ministers and the censorate and provincial offices, every bureau stands empty; of the nine ministers at the Southern Capital only two remain.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said again: "From the Grand Secretariat down through the nine ministries, the censorate, and the provincial offices, every bureau stands empty; of Nanjing's nine ministries only two posts remain filled.

sentences.zh: 天下方面大吏，去秋至今，未嘗用一人。

translations.literal: Among the great regional officials of the realm, from last autumn until now not a single person has been appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Among the realm's regional governors, not one appointment has been made from last autumn until now.

sentences.zh: 陛下萬事不理，以為天下長如此，臣恐禍端一發，不可收也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty attends to nothing, thinking the realm will long remain thus; your servant fears that once trouble breaks out it cannot be contained.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty attends to nothing, as though the realm could long remain thus; I fear that once trouble breaks out it cannot be contained.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不省。

translations.literal: The emperor again took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Again the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 四十年春，向高以歷代帝王享國四十年以上者，自三代迄今止十君，勸帝力行新政。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fortieth year Xianggao noted that among emperors of successive dynasties who had enjoyed the realm for more than forty years, from the Three Dynasties to the present there were only ten rulers, and urged the emperor vigorously to enact new policies.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Wanli 40 (1612) Xianggao observed that from the Three Dynasties to the present only ten rulers had held the throne for more than forty years, and urged the emperor to press forward with real reform.

sentences.zh: 因復以用人行政請，亦不報。

translations.literal: He again petitioned on employing men and administering affairs, and again received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He again petitioned on appointments and governance, and again received no answer.

sentences.zh: 向高誌不行，無月不求去，帝輒優旨勉留。

translations.literal: Xianggao's aims could not be carried out; not a month passed without his asking to leave, yet the emperor each time issued gracious edicts urging him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: With his aims blocked, Xianggao asked to resign nearly every month, yet the emperor each time graciously urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 向高復言：「臣進退可置不問，而百僚必不可盡空，臺諫必不可盡廢，諸方巡按必不可不代。

translations.literal: Xianggao again said: "Your servant's coming or going may be set aside, but the hundred officials must not all be left vacant, the censorate must not all be abolished, and the touring inspectors of the regions must not all go unreplaced.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said again: "Whether I stay or go may be set aside, but the ministries must not all stand empty, the censorate must not be abandoned, and regional inspectors must not all go unreplaced.

sentences.zh: 中外離心，輦轂肘腋間，怨聲憤盈，禍機不測，而陛下務與臣下隔絕。

translations.literal: Court and country are estranged in heart; within the capital's very precincts resentment and anger overflow, and calamity may strike unpredictably—yet Your Majesty strives to cut yourself off from your ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country have lost heart for one another; within the capital itself resentment runs high and disaster may strike at any moment—yet Your Majesty strives to cut yourself off from your ministers.

sentences.zh: 帷幄不得關其忠，六曹不得舉其職，舉天下無一可信之人，而自以為神明之妙用，臣恐自古聖帝明王無此法也。」

translations.literal: The inner council cannot convey their loyalty, the six ministries cannot perform their duties, and throughout the realm there is not one person to be trusted—yet Your Majesty deems this divine subtlety; your servant fears that from antiquity no sage emperor or enlightened king has had such a method."
translations.idiomatic: Your inner council cannot reach you with loyal counsel, the six ministries cannot do their work, and under heaven there is no one left to trust—yet Your Majesty calls this divine subtlety; I fear no sage ruler in history has ever governed thus."

sentences.zh: 先是，向高疾，閣中無人，章奏就其家擬旨者一月。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xianggao was ill and there was no one in the Grand Secretariat, memorials had their rescripts drafted at his home for a month.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xianggao fell ill and the Grand Secretariat stood empty, rescripts were drafted at his home for a month.

sentences.zh: 及是，向高堅臥益久，即家擬旨如前，論者以為非體，向高亦自言其非，堅乞去。

translations.literal: By this time Xianggao lay abed even longer; rescripts were again drafted at his home as before. Critics held this improper, and Xianggao himself acknowledged the impropriety and firmly begged to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Now he lay abed even longer, and rescripts were again drafted at his home as before. Critics called this improper; Xianggao himself acknowledged it and firmly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝卒不命他相，遣鴻臚官慰留。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately did not appoint another chief minister and sent an official of the Court of State Ceremonial to console him and urge him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still would not appoint another chief minister and sent an official of the Court of State Ceremonial to console him and urge him to remain.

sentences.zh: 至帝萬壽節，始起視事。

translations.literal: Only at the emperor's birthday did he rise to attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the emperor's birthday did he rise and return to duty.

sentences.zh: 其後，向高主癸丑會試，章奏皆送闈中，尤異事云。

translations.literal: Thereafter Xianggao presided over the guichou metropolitan examination; all memorials were sent into the examination compound—an especially unusual matter indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he presided over the guichou metropolitan examination, and all memorials were sent into the examination compound—an especially unusual practice.

sentences.zh: 帝考選科道七十餘人，命久不下。

translations.literal: The emperor examined and selected more than seventy censors and investigating censors, but the appointments long went unissued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had examined and selected more than seventy censors and investigating censors, but the appointments long went unissued.

sentences.zh: 向高懇請數十疏，越二年乃下。

translations.literal: Xianggao earnestly petitioned in dozens of memorials; only after two years were they issued.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao petitioned earnestly in dozens of memorials; only after two years were the appointments issued.

sentences.zh: 言官既多，攻擊紛起。

translations.literal: Once the censors were numerous, attacks and counterattacks arose in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: With so many censors in place, attacks and counterattacks multiplied.

sentences.zh: 帝心厭之，章悉留中。

translations.literal: The emperor grew weary in heart and kept all memorials within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew weary of it and kept all memorials within the palace.

sentences.zh: 向高請盡付所司，定其去留。

translations.literal: Xianggao asked that they all be sent to the relevant offices to decide who should stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao asked that they all be sent to the relevant offices to decide who should stay or go.

sentences.zh: 因言：「大臣者，小臣之綱。

translations.literal: He added: "Great ministers are the guiding net for lesser officials.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Great ministers are the guiding net for lesser officials.

sentences.zh: 今六卿止趙煥一人，而都御史十年不補，彈壓無人，人心何由戢？」

translations.literal: Now among the six ministers only Zhao Huan remains, while the censor-in-chief has gone unfilled for ten years; with no one to restrain and suppress, how can popular feeling be quieted?
translations.idiomatic: Now among the six ministers only Zhao Huan remains, while the censor-in-chief has gone unfilled for ten years; with no one to enforce discipline, how can popular feeling be quieted?

sentences.zh: 帝但責言官妄言，而大僚迄不補。

translations.literal: The emperor only blamed the censors for reckless speech, while high offices to the end were not filled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor only blamed the censors for reckless speech, while senior posts still went unfilled.

sentences.zh: 向高請增置閣臣，章至百餘上，帝始用方從哲、吳道南。

translations.literal: Xianggao asked to add Grand Secretaries; memorials reached more than a hundred before the emperor at last appointed Fang Congzhe and Wu Daonan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao asked for additional Grand Secretaries; after more than a hundred memorials the emperor at last appointed Fang Congzhe and Wu Daonan.

sentences.zh: 向高疏謝，因引退，優詔不允。

translations.literal: Xianggao submitted a memorial of thanks and thereupon withdrew; gracious edicts did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao submitted thanks and tried to withdraw; gracious edicts refused.

sentences.zh: 四十二年二月，皇太后崩。

translations.literal: In the second month of the forty-second year the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wanli 42 (1614) the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 三月，福王之國。

translations.literal: In the third month the Prince of Fu went to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Prince of Fu departed for his fief.

sentences.zh: 向高乞歸益數，章十餘上。

translations.literal: Xianggao begged to return home with increasing frequency, submitting more than ten memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao begged to return home with growing urgency, submitting more than ten memorials.

sentences.zh: 至八月，允其去。

translations.literal: By the eighth month his departure was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month his departure was finally granted.

sentences.zh: 向高以三載考績，進太子太保、文淵閣大學士；

translations.literal: At his triennial performance review Xianggao was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth;
translations.idiomatic: At his triennial review he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth;

sentences.zh: 敘延綏戰功，加少保兼太子太保，改戶部尚書、武英殿；

translations.literal: for narrating military achievements in Yan-sui he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian and concurrent Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and made minister of Revenue in the Hall of Martial Glory;
translations.idiomatic: for reporting military achievements in Yan-sui he was made Junior Guardian and concurrent Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Glory;

sentences.zh: 一品三載滿，加少傅兼太子太傅，改吏部尚書、建極殿。

translations.literal: when his first-rank term of three years was complete he was made Junior Mentor and concurrent Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to minister of Personnel in the Hall of Establishing the Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: when his first-rank term was complete he was made Junior Mentor and concurrent Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Establishing the Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 至是，命加少師兼太子太師，賜白金百，彩幣四，表裏大紅坐蟒一襲，遣行人護歸。

translations.literal: At this time he was ordered given the additional title of Junior Preceptor and concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, granted one hundred taels of white silver, four sets of colored silks, one suit of grand red sitting-python robes inside and out, and an envoy was dispatched to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure he was made Junior Preceptor and concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, granted one hundred taels of silver, four sets of colored silks, a grand red python robe, and an envoy to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 向高在相位，務調劑群情，輯和異同。

translations.literal: While Xianggao held the chief ministership, he strove to mediate among the multitude and harmonize differences.
translations.idiomatic: While chief minister, Xianggao strove to mediate among factions and harmonize differences.

sentences.zh: 然其時黨論已大起，御史鄭繼芳力攻給事中王元翰，左右兩人者相角。

translations.literal: Yet by then factional debate had greatly arisen; censor Zheng Jifang fiercely attacked supervising secretary Wang Yuanhan, and the two wings of left and right contended.
translations.idiomatic: Yet factional strife was already rising; Censor Zheng Jifang fiercely attacked Supervising Secretary Wang Yuanhan, and the two wings clashed.

sentences.zh: 向高請盡下諸疏，敕部院評曲直，罪其論議顛倒者一二人，以警其餘，帝不報。

translations.literal: Xianggao asked that all memorials be issued, instructing the ministries and courts to judge right and wrong and punish one or two whose arguments were perverse as a warning to the rest; the emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao asked that all memorials be circulated, the ministries instructed to judge right and wrong, and one or two whose arguments were perverse punished as a warning; the emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 諸臣既無所見得失，益樹黨相攻。

translations.literal: Since the officials could see no judgment of right and wrong, they all the more formed factions and attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: With no official judgment of right and wrong, officials only formed factions and attacked one another more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又爭李三才之事，黨勢乃成。

translations.literal: Before long they disputed again over Li Sancai, and factional power then took shape.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they clashed again over Li Sancai, and factional power took shape.

sentences.zh: 無錫顧憲成家居，講學東林書院，朝士爭慕與遊。

translations.literal: Gu Xiancheng of Wuxi lived at home, lecturing at the Donglin Academy; court officials vied to admire and associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xiancheng of Wuxi lived at home, lecturing at the Donglin Academy, and court officials vied to study with him.

sentences.zh: 三才被攻，憲成貽書向高暨尚書孫丕揚，訟其賢。

translations.literal: When Sancai came under attack, Xiancheng wrote to Xianggao and Minister Sun Piyang pleading his worth.
translations.idiomatic: When Sancai came under attack, Xiancheng wrote to Xianggao and Minister Sun Piyang pleading his worth.

sentences.zh: 會辛亥京察，攻三才者劉國縉以他過掛察典，喬應甲亦用年例出外，其黨大嘩。

translations.literal: At the xinhai capital evaluation, Liu Guojin, who had attacked Sancai, was caught in the evaluation roster for other faults, and Qiao Yingjia was also sent out by seniority rule; their faction was greatly uproarious.
translations.idiomatic: At the xinhai capital evaluation, Liu Guojin, who had attacked Sancai, was caught in the evaluation roster for other faults, and Qiao Yingjia was also sent out by seniority rule; their faction erupted in protest.

sentences.zh: 向高以大體持之，察典得無撓，而兩黨之爭遂不可解。

translations.literal: Xianggao held to the larger principle, and the evaluation roster was not disturbed, but the struggle between the two factions then became irreconcilable.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao held to the larger principle and the evaluation stood, but the struggle between the two factions became irreconcilable.

sentences.zh: 及後，齊、楚、浙黨人攻東林殆盡。

translations.literal: Later, the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factionalists attacked the Donglin faction nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions attacked the Donglin faction nearly to extinction.

sentences.zh: 浸尋至天啟時，王紹徽等撰所謂《東林點將錄》，令魏忠賢按氏名逐朝士。

translations.literal: Gradually, by the Tianqi reign, Wang Shaohui and others compiled the so-called Record of Donglin Generals, having Wei Zhongxian pursue court officials by name.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianqi reign Wang Shaohui and others had compiled the so-called Record of Donglin Generals, enabling Wei Zhongxian to pursue court officials by name.

sentences.zh: 以向高嘗右東林，指目為黨魁云。

translations.literal: Because Xianggao had once favored the Donglin faction, he was pointed at as factional chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xianggao had once favored the Donglin faction, he was singled out as its chieftain.

sentences.zh: 向高歸六年，光宗立，特詔召還。

translations.literal: Six years after Xianggao returned home, when Emperor Guangzong ascended, a special edict summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Six years after his return, when Emperor Guangzong ascended, a special edict summoned him back.

sentences.zh: 未幾，熹宗立，復賜敕趨之。

translations.literal: Before long, when Emperor Xizong ascended, an imperial letter again urged him to hurry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when Emperor Xizong ascended, an imperial letter again urged him to hurry.

sentences.zh: 屢辭，不得命。

translations.literal: He repeatedly declined but could not obtain permission.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly declined but could not obtain permission.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年十月還朝，復為首輔。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianqi he returned to court and again became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tianqi 1 (1621) he returned to court and again became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 言：「臣事皇祖八年，章奏必發臣擬。

translations.literal: He said: "Your servant served the late emperor for eight years; memorials were always issued from drafts I prepared.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "I served your grandfather for eight years; memorials were always issued from drafts I prepared.

sentences.zh: 即上意所欲行，亦遣中使傳諭。

translations.literal: Even when the late emperor's intent wished something carried out, a palace messenger was still sent to convey the instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Even when your grandfather wished something done, a palace messenger was sent to convey the instruction.

sentences.zh: 事有不可，臣力爭，皇祖多曲聽，不欲中出一旨。

translations.literal: When something could not be done, your servant strove in dispute, and the late emperor often bent to listen, unwilling to issue a single edict from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When something could not be done, I argued forcefully, and your grandfather often listened; he was unwilling to issue a single edict from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 陛下虛懷恭己，信任輔臣，然間有宣傳滋疑議。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is open-minded and reverent, trusting your assisting ministers, yet occasionally palace announcements breed suspicion and debate.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is open-minded and trusting of your ministers, yet occasional palace announcements breed suspicion.

sentences.zh: 宜慎重綸音，凡事令臣等擬上。」

translations.literal: You ought carefully to weigh imperial pronouncements and have us ministers draft everything for submission.
translations.idiomatic: You ought weigh imperial pronouncements carefully and have us ministers draft everything for submission.

sentences.zh: 帝優旨報聞。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with gracious words acknowledging the report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied graciously.

sentences.zh: 旋納向高請，發帑金二百萬，為東西用兵之需。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor accepted Xianggao's request and issued two million taels from the treasury for military needs east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor accepted Xianggao's request and issued two million taels from the treasury for campaigns east and west.

sentences.zh: 熹宗初政，群賢滿朝，天下欣欣望治。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xizong's reign worthy men filled the court, and all under heaven looked eagerly for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xizong's reign worthy men filled the court, and the realm looked eagerly for good governance.

sentences.zh: 然帝本沖年，不能辨忠佞。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor was young in years and could not distinguish loyal from treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor was still young and could not distinguish loyal from treacherous men.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢、客氏漸竊威福，構殺太監王安，以次逐吏部尚書周嘉謨及言官倪思輝等。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian and Lady Ke gradually usurped power and favor, framed and killed the eunuch Wang An, and in succession drove out Minister of Personnel Zhou Jiamo and the censor Ni Sihui and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian and Lady Ke gradually usurped power, framed and killed the eunuch Wang An, and in succession drove out Minister Zhou Jiamo and Censor Ni Sihui and others.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉一燝亦力求去。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Yijing also strove forcefully to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Yijing also strove to resign.

sentences.zh: 向高言：「客氏出復入，而一燝顧命大臣不得比保姆，致使人揣摩於奧穾不可知之地，其漸當防。」

translations.literal: Xianggao said: "Lady Ke left and returned, yet Yijing, a entrusted minister on the deathbed, could not compare with a wet nurse—causing people to speculate in the unknowable recesses of the inner palace; this trend ought to be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said: "Lady Ke left and returned, yet Yijing, an entrusted minister on the deathbed, could not compare with a wet nurse—leading people to speculate in the unknowable recesses of the inner palace; this trend must be checked.

sentences.zh: 忠賢見向高疏刺己，恨甚。

translations.literal: Zhongxian, seeing that Xianggao's memorial stabbed at him, hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian, seeing that Xianggao's memorial targeted him, hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 既而刑部尚書王紀削籍，禮部尚書孫慎行、都御史鄒元標先後被攻致仕去。

translations.literal: Then Minister of Punishments Wang Ji was struck from the rolls, while Ministers of Rites Sun Shenxing and Censor-in-Chief Zou Yuanbiao were successively attacked into retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Then Minister of Punishments Wang Ji was struck from the rolls, while Ministers of Rites Sun Shenxing and Censor-in-Chief Zou Yuanbiao were successively attacked into retirement.

sentences.zh: 向高爭不得，因請與元標同罷。

translations.literal: Xianggao could not prevail in dispute and thereupon asked to resign together with Yuanbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao could not prevail and asked to resign together with Yuanbiao.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，而忠賢益恨向高。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen, and Zhongxian hated Xianggao all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, and Zhongxian hated Xianggao all the more.

sentences.zh: 向高為人光明忠厚，有德量，好扶植善類。

translations.literal: Xianggao as a man was open and bright, loyal and generous, with moral capacity, and fond of supporting worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao was open, loyal, and generous, with moral stature and a fondness for supporting worthy men.

sentences.zh: 再入相，事沖主，不能謇直如神宗時，然猶數有匡救。

translations.literal: Entering the chief ministership a second time, serving a young sovereign, he could not be as blunt and upright as in Shenzong's time, yet he still often had corrective saves.
translations.idiomatic: Serving a second time under a young sovereign, he could not be as blunt as under Shenzong, yet he still often intervened to save others.

sentences.zh: 給事中章允儒請減上供袍服。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhang Yunru asked to reduce imperial tribute robes and garments.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Yunru asked to reduce imperial tribute robes and garments.

sentences.zh: 奄人激帝怒，命廷杖。

translations.literal: Eunuchs provoked the emperor's anger, and he ordered court beating.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs provoked the emperor's anger, and he ordered a court beating.

sentences.zh: 向高論救者再，乃奪俸一年。

translations.literal: Xianggao argued twice for his rescue; only then was the punishment reduced to one year's salary forfeiture.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao argued twice for his rescue; only then was the punishment reduced to forfeiture of one year's salary.

sentences.zh: 御史帥眾指斥宮禁，奄人請帝出之外，以向高救免。

translations.literal: Censor Shuai Zhong denounced the inner palace; eunuchs asked the emperor to banish him abroad, but Xianggao rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shuai Zhong denounced the inner palace; eunuchs asked the emperor to banish him, but Xianggao rescued him.

sentences.zh: 給事中傅櫆救王紀，將貶謫，亦以向高言僅奪俸。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Fu Huai rescued Wang Ji; about to be demoted and exiled, he too through Xianggao's words only had salary forfeited.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Fu Huai defended Wang Ji; facing demotion and exile, he too was spared through Xianggao's intervention with only salary forfeited.

sentences.zh: 紀既罷去，御史吳甡、王祚昌薦之，部議以故官召。

translations.literal: After Ji had left office, censors Wu Shen and Wang Zuochang recommended him; the ministry deliberated to summon him by his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji left office, Censors Wu Shen and Wang Zuochang recommended him; the ministry deliberated recalling him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 忠賢怒，將重譴文選郎，向高亦救免。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was angry and was about to heavily punish the personnel selection director; Xianggao again rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was furious and was about to punish the personnel selection director severely; Xianggao again rescued him.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳良訓疏譏權奄，忠賢摘其疏中「國運將終」語，命下詔獄，窮治主使。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Chen Liangxun in a memorial mocked the powerful eunuch; Zhongxian seized the phrase in his memorial that "the nation's fortune is nearing its end" and ordered him sent to the imperial prison to pursue thoroughly who was behind it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Liangxun mocked the powerful eunuch in a memorial; Zhongxian seized the phrase "the nation's fortune is nearing its end" and ordered him to the imperial prison to find who was behind it.

sentences.zh: 向高以去就爭，乃奪俸而止。

translations.literal: Xianggao contested with threats to resign or stay; only then was the punishment reduced to salary forfeiture and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao threatened to resign over it; only then was the punishment reduced to salary forfeiture.

sentences.zh: 熊廷弼、王化貞論死，言官勸帝速決。

translations.literal: Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen were sentenced to death; censors urged the emperor to decide quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen were sentenced to death; censors urged the emperor to decide quickly.

sentences.zh: 向高請俟法司覆奏，帝從之。

translations.literal: Xianggao asked to await the judicial offices' review and resubmission; the emperor complied.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao asked to await the judicial review; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 有請括天下布政司、府、州、縣庫藏盡輸京師者，向高言：「郡邑藏已竭，藩庫稍餘。

translations.literal: There was a proposal to sweep the treasuries of all provincial administrations, prefectures, departments, and counties and transport everything to the capital; Xianggao said: "County and prefectural stores are already exhausted; only provincial treasuries have slight surplus.
translations.idiomatic: When someone proposed sweeping all provincial, prefectural, and county treasuries and shipping everything to the capital, Xianggao said: "County and prefectural stores are already exhausted; only provincial treasuries have any surplus.

sentences.zh: 倘盡括之，猝有如山東白蓮教之亂，何以應之？」

translations.literal: If everything is swept away, should suddenly there arise disorder like the White Lotus sect rebellion in Shandong, how will you respond?
translations.idiomatic: If you sweep them bare, how will you respond if something like the White Lotus rebellion in Shandong breaks out suddenly?

sentences.zh: 帝皆不納。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted none of it.

sentences.zh: 忠賢既默恨向高，而其時朝士與忠賢抗者率倚向高。

translations.literal: Zhongxian already harbored silent hatred for Xianggao, and at that time court officials who resisted Zhongxian mostly relied on Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian already hated Xianggao in silence, and court officials who resisted him mostly relied on Xianggao.

sentences.zh: 忠賢乃時毛舉細故，責向高以困之。

translations.literal: Zhongxian then from time to time picked at petty matters and blamed Xianggao to wear him down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian then picked at petty matters and blamed Xianggao to wear him down.

sentences.zh: 向高數求去。

translations.literal: Xianggao repeatedly asked to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，給事中傅櫆劾左光斗、魏大中交通汪文言，招權納賄，命下文言詔獄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, supervising secretary Fu Huai impeached Zuo Guangdou and Wei Dazhong for associating with Wang Wenyuan, usurping power and taking bribes; the emperor ordered Wenyuan sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Supervising Secretary Fu Huai impeached Zuo Guangdou and Wei Dazhong for associating with Wang Wenyuan, usurping power and taking bribes; the emperor ordered Wenyuan to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 向高言：「文言內閣辦事，實臣具題。

translations.literal: Xianggao said: "Wenyuan handled affairs in the Grand Secretariat; in fact your servant submitted the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said: "Wenyuan handled affairs in the Grand Secretariat; I myself submitted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 光斗等交文言事曖昧，臣用文言顯然。

translations.literal: Guangdou and others' association with Wenyuan is obscure, while your servant's use of Wenyuan is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdou's association with Wenyuan is obscure; my use of him is obvious.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下止罪臣，而稍寬其他，以消縉紳之禍。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to punish only your servant and be somewhat lenient toward the others, to dispel calamity among the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to punish only me and be lenient toward the others, to avert disaster among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 因力求速罷。

translations.literal: He thereupon strove forcefully for swift resignation.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon pressed urgently to resign.

sentences.zh: 當是時，忠賢欲大逞，憚眾正盈朝，伺隙動。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongxian wished to unleash himself fully but feared that upright men filled the court; he watched for an opening to act.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhongxian wished to act freely but feared the upright men who filled the court; he watched for an opening.

sentences.zh: 得櫆疏喜甚，欲藉是羅織東林，終憚向高舊臣，並光斗等不罪，止罪文言。

translations.literal: Receiving Huai's memorial he was greatly pleased and wished to use it to entangle the Donglin faction; in the end he still feared Xianggao as an old minister, and neither Guangdou nor the others were punished—only Wenyuan was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted with Huai's memorial, he wished to use it to entangle the Donglin faction; in the end he still feared Xianggao as an old minister, and neither Guangdou nor the others were punished—only Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 然東林禍自此起。

translations.literal: Yet the Donglin calamity arose from this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Donglin calamity began from this point.

sentences.zh: 至六月，楊漣上疏劾忠賢二十四大罪。

translations.literal: By the sixth month Yang Lian submitted a memorial impeaching Zhongxian for twenty-four great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yang Lian submitted a memorial impeaching Zhongxian for twenty-four great crimes.

sentences.zh: 向高謂事且決裂，深以為非。

translations.literal: Xianggao said the affair would soon rupture and deeply considered it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao said the affair would soon rupture and deeply disapproved.

sentences.zh: 廷臣相繼抗章至數十上，或勸向高下其事，可決勝也。

translations.literal: Court officials successively submitted resisting memorials reaching dozens; some urged Xianggao to issue the matter, saying victory could be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials submitted dozens of resisting memorials; some urged Xianggao to issue Yang's memorial, saying victory was at hand.

sentences.zh: 向高念忠賢未易除，閣臣從中挽回，猶冀無大禍。

translations.literal: Xianggao reflected that Zhongxian was not easily removed; if Grand Secretaries mediated from within, he still hoped there would be no great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao thought Zhongxian was not easily removed; if the Grand Secretaries mediated, he still hoped to avoid great disaster.

sentences.zh: 乃具奏稱忠賢勤勞。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a full memorial saying Zhongxian was diligent and toilsome.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial praising Zhongxian's diligence.

sentences.zh: 朝廷寵待厚，盛滿難居，宜解事權，聽歸私第，保全終始。

translations.literal: The court's favor and treatment were thick; when fullness reaches its peak it is hard to remain—he ought to relinquish administrative power, be permitted to return to his private residence, and preserve beginning and end intact.
translations.idiomatic: The court had favored him richly; at the height of fortune it is hard to remain—he ought to relinquish power, retire to his home, and preserve his good name to the end.

sentences.zh: 忠賢不悅，矯帝旨敘己功勤，累百餘言。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was displeased and forged the emperor's intent to narrate his own merits and diligence in more than a hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was displeased and forged an imperial edict narrating his own merits in more than a hundred words.

sentences.zh: 向高駭曰：「此非奄人所能，必有代為草者。」

translations.literal: Xianggao was alarmed and said: "This is not something a eunuch could do—there must be someone who drafted it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao was alarmed and said: "A eunuch could not have written this—someone must have drafted it for him.

sentences.zh: 探之，則徐大化也。

translations.literal: On investigation it was Xu Dahua.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation showed it was Xu Dahua.

sentences.zh: 忠賢雖憤，猶以外廷勢盛，未敢加害。

translations.literal: Although Zhongxian was furious, he still feared the outer court's power was strong and did not dare to harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Although furious, Zhongxian still feared the outer court's strength and did not dare strike.

sentences.zh: 其黨有導以興大獄者，忠賢意遂決。

translations.literal: His faction had those who guided him to launch a great prosecution; Zhongxian's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: His faction urged him to launch a great prosecution; Zhongxian's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 於是工部郎中萬燝以劾忠賢廷杖，向高力救，不從，死杖下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bureau Director Wan Lian of the Ministry of Works, for impeaching Zhongxian, was beaten at court; Xianggao strove to save him but was not obeyed, and he died under the rods.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Bureau Director Wan Lian of the Ministry of Works, for impeaching Zhongxian, was beaten at court; Xianggao strove to save him in vain, and he died under the rods.

sentences.zh: 無何，御史林汝翥亦以忤奄命廷杖。

translations.literal: Before long, Censor Lin Ruzhu also, for having offended the eunuchs, was ordered to be beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Censor Lin Ruzhu was likewise ordered beaten at court for defying the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 汝翥懼，投遵化巡撫所。

translations.literal: Ruzhu was afraid and fled to the Zunhua grand coordinator's office.
translations.idiomatic: In fear, Ruzhu fled to seek refuge with the grand coordinator of Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 或言汝翥向高甥也，群奄圍其邸大噪。

translations.literal: Some said Ruzhu was Xianggao's nephew by marriage; a mob of eunuchs surrounded his residence and made a great noise.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that Ruzhu was Ye Xianggao's nephew-in-law, a throng of eunuchs surrounded his residence and raised an uproar.

sentences.zh: 向高以時事不可為，乞歸已二十餘疏，至是請益力。

translations.literal: Xianggao, believing the times permitted no achievement, had already submitted more than twenty memorials requesting retirement; at this point he pleaded all the more forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that the times were beyond remedy, Ye Xianggao had already submitted more than twenty memorials asking to retire; now he pressed the request still harder.

sentences.zh: 乃命加太傅，遣行人護歸，所給賜視彜典有加。

translations.literal: He was then ordered promoted to Grand Tutor, an envoy was dispatched to escort him home, and the gifts granted exceeded the ritual norms.
translations.idiomatic: The court then promoted him to Grand Tutor and dispatched an imperial envoy to escort him home; the honors and gifts surpassed the usual ceremonial standards.

sentences.zh: 尋聽辭太傅，有司月給米五石，輿夫八。

translations.literal: Soon he was permitted to decline the Grand Tutorship; the relevant offices monthly supplied him five piculs of rice and eight sedan-chair bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was allowed to decline the Grand Tutorship; the government granted him five piculs of rice per month and eight sedan-bearers.

sentences.zh: 向高既罷去，韓爌、朱國禎相繼為首輔，未久皆罷。

translations.literal: After Xianggao had left office, Han Kuang and Zhu Guozhen successively became chief ministers; before long both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After Ye Xianggao's departure, Han Kuang and Zhu Guozhen served in turn as chief minister, but neither lasted long.

sentences.zh: 居政府者皆小人，清流無所依倚。

translations.literal: Those who held office in the government were all petty men; the clear stream had nothing to lean on.
translations.idiomatic: The government was now filled with lesser men, and the reform-minded officials had no one to rely upon.

sentences.zh: 忠賢首誣殺漣，光斗等次第戮辱，貶削朝士之異己者，善類為一空云。

translations.literal: Zhongxian first had Lian killed on false charges; Guangdou and the others were successively humiliated and executed; court officials who differed from him were demoted or stripped of rank—the good were emptied out entirely, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian first had Yang Lian framed and killed; Zuo Guangdou and others were executed in turn; dissenters were demoted or purged until the ranks of upright officials were virtually emptied.

sentences.zh: 熹宗崩，向高亦以是月卒，年六十有九。

translations.literal: The Xizong emperor died; Xianggao also died in that same month, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianqi Emperor died, Ye Xianggao also passed away that same month, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太師，謚文忠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Wenzhong ("Loyal in Letters").

sentences.zh: 劉一燝

translations.literal: Liu Yijing
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing

sentences.zh: 劉一燝，字季晦，南昌人。

translations.literal: Liu Yijing, styled Jihui, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing, courtesy name Jihui, came from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 父曰材，嘉靖中進士，陜西左布政使。

translations.literal: His father was named Cai; a jinshi of the Jiajing reign, he was left administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Cai, a jinshi of the Jiajing era, had served as left administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十六年，一燝與兄一焜、一煜並舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Wanli, Yijing together with his elder brothers Yikun and Yiyu all passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 16 (1588), Liu Yijing passed the provincial examination together with his elder brothers Yikun and Yiyu.

sentences.zh: 越七年，又與一煜並舉進士。

translations.literal: Seven years later he again passed the jinshi examination together with Yiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later he and Yiyu both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 一焜為考功郎，掌京察。

translations.literal: Yikun served as director in the Bureau of Evaluation and oversaw the capital personnel review.
translations.idiomatic: Yikun served as director in the Bureau of Evaluation and oversaw the Beijing metropolitan evaluation.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫欲庇其私人錢夢臯、鐘兆鬥等，屬一燝為請。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan wished to protect his private associates Qian Menggao, Zhong Zhaodou, and others, and entrusted Yijing to plead on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan sought to shield his protégés Qian Menggao and Zhong Zhaodou, and asked Liu Yijing to intercede for them.

sentences.zh: 一燝謝不可，夢臯等竟以中旨留，由是忤一貫意。

translations.literal: Yijing declined, saying he could not; Menggao and the others were ultimately retained by a palace rescript—thereby offending Yiguan's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing refused; Qian Menggao and the others were kept in office anyway by an edict from within the palace, and Liu thus fell out of Shen Yiguan's favor.

sentences.zh: 尋歷祭酒，詹事，掌翰林院事。

translations.literal: He soon successively served as chancellor of the Directorate of Education, grand secretary of the heir apparent's household, and head of Hanlin Academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served in succession as chancellor of the Directorate of Education, grand secretary of the heir apparent's household, and director of Hanlin Academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 四十五年春，京察，黨人用事，謀逐孫承宗、繆昌期等，一燝力保持得免。

translations.literal: In the spring of the forty-fifth year, during the capital personnel review, factionalists held sway and plotted to drive out Sun Chengzong, Miao Changqi, and others; Yijing strove to preserve them and they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Wanli 45 (1617), during the Beijing evaluation, faction leaders plotted to purge Sun Chengzong and Miao Changqi; Liu Yijing fought to protect them, and they were spared.

sentences.zh: 故事，掌院無滿歲不遷者，一景居四年，始遷禮部右侍郎，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: By precedent, none who headed the academy served a full year without transfer; Yijing held the post four years before he was first transferred to right vice minister of Rites to instruct the Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, directors of the Hanlin Academy were transferred within a year; Liu Yijing served four years before he was finally made right vice minister of Rites and instructor to the Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，擢禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，參預機務，偕何宗彥、韓爌並命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, Yijing was promoted to minister of Rites and concurrent Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion to participate in state affairs, appointed together with He Zongyan and Han Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, Liu Yijing was elevated to minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion to join in state deliberations, in the same edict as He Zongyan and Han Kuang.

sentences.zh: 時內閣止方從哲一人。

translations.literal: At the time the inner cabinet had only Fang Congzhe alone.
translations.idiomatic: At that point the Grand Secretariat consisted of Fang Congzhe alone.

sentences.zh: 萬曆末年，神宗欲用史繼偕、沈纮。

translations.literal: In the closing years of Wanli, Shenzong wished to employ Shi Jijie and Shen Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wanli reign, the Wanli Emperor had intended to recall Shi Jijie and Shen Hong.

sentences.zh: 兩人方在籍，帝命召之。

translations.literal: The two were still in their native places; the emperor ordered them summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were still at home on leave when the emperor ordered them recalled.

sentences.zh: 未及至，帝復命宗彥、一燝、爌。

translations.literal: Before they had arrived, the emperor again appointed Zongyan, Yijing, and Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Before either could reach the capital, the emperor instead appointed He Zongyan, Liu Yijing, and Han Kuang.

sentences.zh: 明日，復命朱國祚及舊輔葉向高。

translations.literal: The next day he again appointed Zhu Guozuo and the former minister Ye Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he also recalled Zhu Guozuo and the veteran minister Ye Xianggao.

sentences.zh: 而宗彥、國祚、向高亦皆在籍，惟一燝、爌入直。

translations.literal: But Zongyan, Guozuo, and Xianggao were all still in their native places; only Yijing and Kuang entered duty at court.
translations.idiomatic: He Zongyan, Zhu Guozuo, and Ye Xianggao were all still at home; only Liu Yijing and Han Kuang took up their posts at court.

sentences.zh: 甫拜命，帝已得疾，一燝偕諸臣召見乾清宮。

translations.literal: As soon as they had received appointment, the emperor was already ill; Yijing together with the other officials was summoned to audience at the Qianqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had they accepted their commissions when the emperor fell ill; Liu Yijing and the other ministers were summoned to audience in the Qianqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 明日九月朔，帝崩。

translations.literal: The next day, the first day of the ninth month, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day—the first day of the ninth month—the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 諸臣入臨畢，一燝詰群奄：「皇長子當柩前即位，今不在，何也？」

translations.literal: After the officials had entered to mourn, Yijing interrogated the eunuchs: "The eldest imperial son ought to ascend the throne before the coffin—he is not here now; why?
translations.idiomatic: After the officials had finished paying respects, Liu Yijing confronted the eunuchs: "The crown prince should succeed before the coffin's presence—where is he now?

sentences.zh: 群奄東西走，不對。

translations.literal: The eunuchs ran east and west and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs scurried about and would not answer.

sentences.zh: 東宮伴讀王安前曰：「為李選侍所匿耳。」

translations.literal: Wang An, the eastern-palace companion reader, stepped forward and said: "He is merely hidden by Lady Li the attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang An, tutor to the crown prince, stepped forward: "Lady Li the concubine-attendant has him hidden away.

sentences.zh: 一燝大聲言：「誰敢匿新天子者？」

translations.literal: Yijing said in a loud voice: "Who would dare hide the new Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing cried out: "Who would dare conceal the new emperor?"

sentences.zh: 安曰：「徐之，公等慎勿退。」

translations.literal: An said: "Wait a moment; you gentlemen take care not to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Wang An said: "Wait—you gentlemen must not leave."

sentences.zh: 遂趨入白選侍。

translations.literal: He thereupon hurried in to inform the attendant.
translations.idiomatic: With that he hurried in to inform Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 選侍頷之，復中悔，挽皇長子裾。

translations.literal: The attendant nodded, then halfway regretted it and grasped the eldest imperial son's robe.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li nodded assent, then changed her mind and seized the crown prince by the hem of his robe.

sentences.zh: 安直前擁抱，疾趨出。

translations.literal: An went straight forward, embraced him, and hurried out at speed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang An rushed forward, swept the boy into his arms, and hurried out.

sentences.zh: 一燝見之，急趨前呼萬歲，捧皇長子左手，英國公張惟賢捧右手，掖升輦。

translations.literal: Yijing seeing this hurried forward, cried "Long live the emperor!" grasped the eldest imperial son's left hand; Zhang Weixian, Duke of Ying, grasped his right hand, and they supported him onto the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this, Liu Yijing rushed forward shouting "Long live the emperor!" He took the crown prince's left hand while Zhang Weixian, Duke of Ying, took his right, and they helped him into the imperial sedan.

sentences.zh: 及門，宮中厲聲呼：「哥兒卻還！」

translations.literal: At the gate, from within the palace a fierce voice cried: "Little brother, come back!
translations.idiomatic: At the gate a shrill voice from within the palace cried: "Little prince, come back!

sentences.zh: 使使追躡者三輩。

translations.literal: Messengers were sent—three parties to pursue and follow.
translations.idiomatic: Three successive groups of messengers were sent in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 一燝傍輦疾行，翼升文華殿，先即東宮位，群臣叩頭呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Yijing walked swiftly beside the palanquin, winged his ascent to the Wenhua Hall, first took the eastern-palace seat; the assembled officials kowtowed and cried long life.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing kept pace with the sedan, escorted the prince to the Wenhua Hall, and had him take the heir apparent's seat; the assembled officials kowtowed and shouted their acclamations.

sentences.zh: 事稍定，選侍猶趨還乾清。

translations.literal: When matters had somewhat settled, the attendant still hurried back to Qianqing.
translations.idiomatic: Once the immediate crisis had passed, Lady Li still tried to hurry back to the Qianqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 時選侍居乾清。

translations.literal: At the time the attendant resided in Qianqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was still lodged in the Qianqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 一燝曰：「乾清不可居，殿下宜暫居慈慶。」

translations.literal: Yijing said: "Qianqing cannot be occupied; Your Highness ought temporarily to reside at Ciqing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing said: "You cannot remain in Qianqing Palace; Your Highness should move temporarily to Ciqing.

sentences.zh: 皇長子心憚選侍，然之。
