translations.literal: The eldest imperial son inwardly feared the attendant and assented.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, still afraid of Lady Li, agreed.

sentences.zh: 一燝語安曰：「主上沖年，無母後。

translations.literal: Yijing said to An: "The sovereign is in tender years and has no proper empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing told Wang An: "The emperor is still a child and has no empress dowager to oversee him.

sentences.zh: 外庭有事，吾受過；

translations.literal: If there are matters in the outer court, I shall bear the blame;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever goes wrong in the outer court, I will take the blame;

sentences.zh: 宮中起居，公等不得辭責。」

translations.literal: the inner palace's daily conduct—you gentlemen cannot evade responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: but for life within the palace, you may not shirk your duties.

sentences.zh: 明日，周嘉謨及左光斗疏請移宮。

translations.literal: The next day Zhou Jiamo and Zuo Guangdou submitted memorials requesting the move of palace residence.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhou Jiamo and Zuo Guangdou submitted memorials demanding that Lady Li be moved from the palace.

sentences.zh: 時首輔從哲徘徊其間，已，又欲緩移宮。

translations.literal: At the time the chief minister Congzhe wavered among them; afterward he also wished to delay the move of residence.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Fang Congzhe wavered on the issue and soon wished to slow the move.

sentences.zh: 一燝曰：「本朝故事，仁聖，嫡母也，移慈慶；

translations.literal: Yijing said: "By our dynasty's precedent, Rensheng, the lawful mother, moved to Ciqing;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing said: "By dynastic precedent, Empress Dowager Rensheng, as the legitimate mother, moved to Ciqing;

sentences.zh: 慈聖，生母也，移慈寧。

translations.literal: Cisheng, the birth mother, moved to Cining.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cisheng, as the birth mother, moved to Cining.

sentences.zh: 今何日，可姑緩耶？」

translations.literal: What day is it that we can for the moment delay?
translations.idiomatic: On what grounds can we delay now?

sentences.zh: 初五日，偕同官請即日降旨，佇立宮門以俟。

translations.literal: On the fifth day he together with his fellow officials requested that an edict be issued that very day, standing at the palace gate to wait.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day he and his colleagues asked for an immediate edict and stood waiting at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 選侍不得已，移噦鸞宮，天子復還乾清，事始大定。

translations.literal: The attendant had no choice; she moved to Huanyuan Palace; the Son of Heaven returned to Qianqing, and matters at last greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li had no choice but to move to Huanyuan Palace; the emperor returned to Qianqing, and the succession crisis was finally resolved.

sentences.zh: 帝既踐阼，從哲被劾在告，一燝遂當國，與爌相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had taken the throne, Congzhe was impeached and on leave; Yijing thereupon held the state, and he and Kuang got along very happily.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's accession, Fang Congzhe was impeached and left on sick leave; Liu Yijing thus directed the government and worked in close harmony with Han Kuang.

sentences.zh: 念內廷惟王安力衛新天子，乃引與共事。

translations.literal: Reflecting that within the inner court only Wang An had exerted himself to protect the new Son of Heaven, he brought him in to handle affairs together.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing that Wang An had been the eunuch who had forcefully protected the new emperor, Liu Yijing brought him into joint administration.

sentences.zh: 安亦傾心向之。

translations.literal: An also devoted his heart to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang An in turn gave Liu Yijing his full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 所奏請，無不從。

translations.literal: Whatever they submitted in request, there was nothing not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever they proposed, the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 發內帑，抑近侍，搜遺逸，舊德宿齒布滿九列，中外欣欣望治焉。

translations.literal: Inner treasuries were opened, close attendants were checked, lost talents were sought; old worthies and long-serving elders filled the nine ranks—within and without alike rejoiced and looked toward good governance.
translations.idiomatic: They tapped the inner treasury, reined in palace favorites, sought out neglected talent, and filled the high offices with veteran statesmen; court and country alike rejoiced and looked forward to a new era of order.

sentences.zh: 明年，天啟改元，沈陽失。

translations.literal: The next year, with the Tianqi reign's change of era, Shenyang was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Tianqi reign began—and Shenyang fell.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多請復用熊廷弼。

translations.literal: Many court officials requested that Xiong Tingbi be reemployed.
translations.idiomatic: Many at court urged that Xiong Tingbi be brought back.

sentences.zh: 一燝亦言：「廷弼守遼一載，殘疆宴然，不知何故翦除。

translations.literal: Yijing also said: "Tingbi held Liaodong one year; the remnant territory was tranquil—who knows for what reason he was cut down?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing also argued: "Xiong Tingbi held Liaodong for a year and kept what remained of the frontier secure—why ever was he removed?

sentences.zh: 及下廷議，又皆畏懼，不敢異同。

translations.literal: When the matter was referred to court deliberation, again all were afraid and dared not differ or agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the matter went to deliberation, everyone was too frightened to speak out of turn.

sentences.zh: 嗣後軍國大事，陛下當毅然主持，賴諸臣洗心滌慮，悉破雷同附和，其憂國奉公。」

translations.literal: Henceforth on great military and state affairs, Your Majesty should resolutely take charge; rely on your ministers to cleanse their hearts and wash their thoughts, thoroughly break uniform echoing and assent, and devote themselves to the state and public service.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth on matters of war and state, Your Majesty must decide resolutely. I look to your ministers to set aside fear and faction, stop echoing one another, and truly serve the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝優旨褒答。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with gracious edicts of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with an edict of warm praise.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔盡謫前排廷弼者姚宗文等官。

translations.literal: Soon an edict demoted all who had previously denounced Tingbi—officials such as Yao Zongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict dismissed all the officials who had led the charge against Xiong Tingbi, including Yao Zongwen.

sentences.zh: 言路多怨一燝。

translations.literal: The memorialists largely resented Yijing.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial and memorialist faction largely resented Liu Yijing for this.

sentences.zh: 一燝嘗言：「任天下事者，惟六官。

translations.literal: Yijing once said: "Those who bear responsibility for the affairs of the realm are only the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing once said: "The six ministries alone should bear responsibility for governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 言路張，則六官無實政。

translations.literal: When the memorialist path is expansive, the Six Ministries have no real administration.
translations.idiomatic: When memorialists hold too much sway, the six ministries cannot govern in earnest.

sentences.zh: 善治天下者，俾六官任事，言路得繩其愆，言官陳事，政府得裁其是，則天下治。」

translations.literal: One who governs the realm well makes the Six Ministries bear tasks; the memorialist path may check their faults; when memorial officials present affairs, the government may judge their rightness—then the realm is governed.
translations.idiomatic: Good governance means letting the six ministries do the work while the memorialists hold them accountable. Memorialists may raise issues; the government may judge them—but only then is the realm truly governed.

sentences.zh: 於是一切條奏悉下部議，有不經者，詔格之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all itemized memorials were entirely sent down to the ministries for deliberation; those that were unsound were rejected by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every detailed memorial went to the ministries for review; edicts blocked those that were irregular.

sentences.zh: 初，選侍將移宮，其內豎李進忠、劉朝、田詔等盜內府秘藏，過乾清門仆，金寶墮地。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the attendant was about to move palace, her inner eunuchs Li Jinzhong, Liu Chao, Tian Zhao, and others stole secret treasures of the inner palace; passing Qianqing Gate one fell; gold and jewels dropped to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Lady Li prepared to move out, her eunuchs Li Jinzhong, Liu Chao, and Tian Zhao stole treasures from the inner storehouse; passing through Qianqing Gate one of them stumbled and jewels spilled onto the ground.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，悉下法司，案治甚急。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent them all to the judicial offices; the investigation and punishment were very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and handed them all over to the judiciary for urgent prosecution.

sentences.zh: 群奄懼，構蜚語，言帝薄先朝妃嬪，致選侍移宮日，跣足投井，以搖惑外廷。

translations.literal: The eunuchs were afraid and fabricated slanderous talk, saying the emperor slighted the previous reign's consorts, causing the attendant on the day of her move to go barefoot and throw herself into a well, to shake and mislead the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the eunuchs spread rumors that the emperor despised his predecessors' consorts, forcing Lady Li—on the day of her eviction—to go barefoot and throw herself into a well, hoping to sway the outer court.

sentences.zh: 御史賈繼春遂上安選侍書。

translations.literal: Censor Jia Jichun thereupon submitted a memorial calming the attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jia Jichun submitted a memorial pleading on Lady Li's behalf.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書黃克纘、給事中李春曄、御史王業浩輩張大其辭，欲脫盜奄罪。

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Huang Kezuan, Secretariat Receiver Li Chunye, Censor Wang Yehao, and their party inflated the language, wishing to absolve the thieving eunuchs of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Huang Kezuan, Li Chunye of the Secretariat, Censor Wang Yehao, and others inflated the charges in language designed to exonerate the thieving eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 帝惡繼春妄言，且疑其有黨，將嚴譴之。

translations.literal: The emperor hated Jichun's reckless speech and also suspected he had a faction; he was about to severely punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loathed Jia Jichun's reckless talk and suspected him of factional backing; he was about to punish him severely.

sentences.zh: 一燝謂天子新即位，輒疑臣下朋黨，異時奸人乘間，士大夫必受其禍。

translations.literal: Yijing said that the Son of Heaven had newly ascended the throne; to at once suspect ministers of faction—if in time evil men seized the gap, literati would surely suffer calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing argued that a newly enthroned emperor who immediately suspected his officials of faction would one day leave scholars vulnerable when schemers moved in.

sentences.zh: 乃具疏開帝意，為繼春解，而反覆言朋黨無實。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a full memorial to open the emperor's mind, exonerating Jichun, and repeatedly saying faction had no reality.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a detailed memorial to dissuade the emperor, defended Jia Jichun, and insisted repeatedly that talk of faction was groundless.

sentences.zh: 繼春得削籍去。

translations.literal: Jichun was merely stripped of registry and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Jichun was merely stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 御史張慎言、高弘圖疏救繼春，帝欲並罪，亦以一燝言而止。

translations.literal: Censors Zhang Shenyan and Gao Hongtu submitted memorials to rescue Jichun; the emperor wished to punish them together, but this too was stopped on Yijing's word.
translations.idiomatic: When Censors Zhang Shenyan and Gao Hongtu memorialized in Jia Jichun's defense, the emperor wanted to punish them too—but again Liu Yijing intervened.

sentences.zh: 帝憾選侍甚，必欲誅盜奄。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly resented the attendant and surely wished to execute the thieving eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still bore deep resentment toward Lady Li and was determined to have the thieving eunuchs put to death.

sentences.zh: 王安為司禮，亦惡之。

translations.literal: Wang An as Director of Ceremonial also hated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang An, now head of the Directorate of Ceremonial, also wanted them punished.

sentences.zh: 諸奄百方救，卒不得。

translations.literal: The eunuchs tried every way to save them and in the end could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs tried every means to save them but failed.

sentences.zh: 久而帝漸忘前事，安亦為魏忠賢排死，諸奄乃厚賄忠賢為地，而上疏辨冤。

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor gradually forgot the earlier affair; An was also removed to death by Wei Zhongxian; the eunuchs then bribed Zhongxian heavily to make room, and submitted memorials pleading innocence.
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor's anger faded; Wang An was hounded to his death by Wei Zhongxian; the eunuchs then lavished bribes on Zhongxian and submitted memorials pleading their innocence.

sentences.zh: 帝果免朝、詔死，下其疏法司。

translations.literal: The emperor indeed spared Chao and Zhao from death and sent their memorials down to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did spare Liu Chao and Tian Zhao from execution and referred their memorials to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 一燝執奏，詔等議誅久，無可雪，疏直下部，前無此制。

translations.literal: Yijing held his submission, saying Zhao and the others had long been discussed for execution and there was nothing to be cleared; memorials sent straight to the ministries—never before had there been such a procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing objected: Tian Zhao and the others had long been marked for execution and had no case to clear; sending such memorials straight to the ministries broke all precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，下其疏於閣。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice but to send their memorials to the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reluctantly forwarded their memorials to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 一燝復言：「此疏外不由通政司，內不由會極門，例不當擬旨，謹封還原疏。」

translations.literal: Yijing again said: "These memorials, without passing through the Transmission Office without or the Gate of Supreme Harmony within, by precedent ought not receive drafted rescripts; I respectfully seal and return the original memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing replied: "These memorials bypassed the Transmission Office and the Gate of Supreme Harmony; by precedent we may not draft a rescript. I respectfully return the originals.

sentences.zh: 由是忠賢輩大恨，朝等亦竟免死，益任用。

translations.literal: From this Zhongxian and his party greatly hated him; Chao and the others in the end also escaped death and were all the more employed.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Wei Zhongxian and his allies despised Liu Yijing; Liu Chao and the others escaped death after all and gained still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 定陵工成，忠賢欲以為功。

translations.literal: When work on the Dingling tomb was completed, Zhongxian wished to claim it as merit.
translations.idiomatic: When construction of the Dingling mausoleum was finished, Wei Zhongxian sought credit for the achievement.

sentences.zh: 一燝援故事，內臣非司禮掌印及提督陵工不得濫蔭，止擬加恩三等。

translations.literal: Yijing cited precedent: inner servants who were not seal-holding directors of ceremonial or supervisors of tomb work must not receive indiscriminate enfeoffment benefits; he proposed only adding grace by three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing cited precedent: only eunuchs who held the seal of the Directorate of Ceremonial or supervised tomb construction might claim enfeoffment; he proposed only a modest third-degree promotion of honors.

sentences.zh: 諸言官論客氏被謫者，一燝皆疏救，又請出客氏於外。

translations.literal: The various memorialist officials who had criticized Ke Shi and been demoted—Yijing submitted memorials to rescue them all, and also requested that Ke Shi be sent out of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in defense of every censor punished for criticizing Ke Shi, and also asked that she be sent out of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 及言官交章論沈纮，纮疑一燝主之，與忠賢、客氏等比，而齮一燝。

translations.literal: When memorialists submitted successive chapters criticizing Shen Hong, Hong suspected Yijing was behind it; he joined with Zhongxian, Ke Shi, and others to slander Yijing.
translations.idiomatic: When censors submitted a barrage of memorials against Shen Hong, Shen suspected Liu Yijing was directing them; he joined Wei Zhongxian and Ke Shi in working to undermine Liu.

sentences.zh: 一燝持大體，不徇言路意。

translations.literal: Yijing upheld the larger norms and did not defer to the memorialists' wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing held to the larger good and refused to defer to the memorialists.

sentences.zh: 言路頗怨。

translations.literal: The memorialist path was rather resentful.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial faction grew still more resentful toward him.

sentences.zh: 又密窺魏、客等漸用事，一燝勢孤，是年四月，候補御史劉重慶遂力詆一燝不可用。

translations.literal: Again secretly observing that Wei, Ke, and others were gradually wielding power, Yijing's position was isolated; in the fourth month of that year, probationary censor Liu Chongqing then vigorously denounced Yijing as unfit for use.
translations.idiomatic: They also watched in secret as Wei Zhongxian, Ke Shi, and their allies steadily gained influence, leaving Liu Yijing increasingly isolated. That April, probationary censor Liu Chongqing launched a fierce attack declaring Liu unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 帝怒謫重慶。

translations.literal: The emperor in anger demoted Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demoted Liu Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 一燝再論救，不聽。

translations.literal: Yijing again argued to save him; [the emperor] would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing memorialized again to defend him, but the emperor refused to relent.

sentences.zh: 而職方郎中余大成、御史安伸、給事中韋蕃、霍維華交章劾一燝。

translations.literal: Meanwhile bureau director Yu Dacheng, censor An Shen, and supervising secretaries Wei Fan and Huo Weihua submitted successive memorials impeaching Yijing.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Military Appointments Director Yu Dacheng, Censor An Shen, and Supervising Secretaries Wei Fan and Huo Weihua filed successive impeachments against Liu Yijing.

sentences.zh: 帝不問。

translations.literal: The emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 既而維華外轉，其同官孫傑疑一燝屬嘉謨為之，上疏力攻一燝。

translations.literal: Before long Weihua was transferred outward; his colleague Sun Jie suspected Yijing had had Jiamo do it and submitted a memorial vigorously attacking Yijing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huo Weihua was soon transferred to an outside post, his colleague Sun Jie suspected Liu Yijing had engineered it through Jiamo and submitted a fierce memorial against Liu.

sentences.zh: 一燝疏辨求罷。

translations.literal: Yijing submitted a memorial of defense and asked to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing submitted a rebuttal and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝已慰留，給事中侯震旸、御史陳九疇復劾之，並刺其結納王安。

translations.literal: The emperor had already comfortingly retained him; supervising secretary Hou Zhenyong and censor Chen Jiuchou again impeached him, also stabbing at his forming ties with Wang An.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already urged him to stay; Supervising Secretary Hou Zhenyong and Censor Chen Jiuchou impeached him again, accusing him of cultivating ties with Wang An.

sentences.zh: 於是一燝四疏乞歸，忠賢從中主之，傳旨允其去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yijing submitted four memorials begging to retire; Zhongxian from the midst took charge, and an edict was transmitted approving his departure.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing then submitted four memorials begging to retire. Wei Zhongxian steered the outcome from behind the scenes, and an edict was issued approving his departure.

sentences.zh: 先是，從哲去，帝數稱一燝為首輔，一燝不敢當，虛位俟葉向高。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Congzhe departed, the emperor repeatedly called Yijing chief grand secretary; Yijing did not dare accept it and left the seat vacant awaiting Ye Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Fang Congzhe left office, the emperor had repeatedly named Liu Yijing chief grand secretary. Liu demurred, leaving the post vacant while awaiting Ye Xianggao's return.

sentences.zh: 及向高至，入讒言，謂一燝尼己。

translations.literal: When Xianggao arrived, slanders were entered, saying Yijing obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye Xianggao arrived, slanders reached the court claiming Liu Yijing was blocking his path.

sentences.zh: 至是，知其無他，力稱一燝有翼衛功，不可去。

translations.literal: At this point, knowing he had no other design, he forcefully praised Yijing's merits in winging and guarding and said he could not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Ye Xianggao knew Liu had no ulterior motive and vigorously argued that Liu's service in crowning and protecting the emperor made him indispensable.

sentences.zh: 帝復慰留，一燝堅臥不起。

translations.literal: The emperor again comfortingly retained him; Yijing firmly lay ill and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again urged him to stay, but Liu Yijing stubbornly kept to his sickbed.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，疏十二上，乃令乘傳歸。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, after twelve memorials submitted, he was finally ordered to return home by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianqi 2, after twelve memorials, he was at last permitted to return home on official relay transport.

sentences.zh: 既歸，兵部尚書張鶴鳴興奸細杜茂、劉一巘獄，欲指一巘為一燝族，株連之。

translations.literal: After he returned, Minister of War Zhang Heming raised a case on spies Du Mao and Liu Yiyan, wishing to designate Yiyan as Yijing's clansman and implicate him by extension.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yijing retired, War Minister Zhang Heming opened a trial of alleged spies Du Mao and Liu Yiyan, seeking to portray Yiyan as a kinsman of Liu Yijing and implicate him by association.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書王紀不可，遂被斥去，而一燝得白。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Wang Ji would not consent; he was thereupon driven out, and Yijing was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Justice Minister Wang Ji refused to cooperate and was himself forced out, but Liu Yijing was cleared.

sentences.zh: 鶴鳴，一燝向所推轂者也。

translations.literal: Heming was one whom Yijing had formerly pushed forward in the chariot's wheel-hub.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heming was a man Liu Yijing himself had once promoted.

sentences.zh: 已而忠賢大熾，矯旨責一燝誤用廷弼，削官，追奪誥命，勒令養馬。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongxian greatly flared; feigning an edict he blamed Yijing for the misemployment of Tingbi, stripped his office, recovered and seized his patents of nobility, and compelled him to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wei Zhongxian's power surged. Forging an edict, he charged Liu Yijing with wrongly appointing Xiong Tingbi, stripped his rank, revoked his patents of nobility, and reduced him to the disgrace of keeping horses.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，詔復官，遣官存問。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen era was inaugurated, an edict restored his office and sent officials to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign, an edict restored his rank and dispatched officials to visit him.

sentences.zh: 一燝在位，累加少傅、太子太傅、吏部尚書、中極殿大學士。

translations.literal: While Yijing held office, he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Tutor, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Central Peak Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure Liu Yijing had risen through Junior Tutor, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Central Peak Hall.

sentences.zh: 八年卒，贈少師。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died; Junior Preceptor was posthumously conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year and was posthumously granted the title Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚文端。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, the posthumous title Wenduan was bestowed in retrospect.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted the title Wenduan, "Cultivated and Upright."

sentences.zh: 兄 一焜 一煜

translations.literal: Elder brothers: Yikun, Yiyu.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers were Liu Yikun and Liu Yiyu.

sentences.zh: 一焜，字元丙。

translations.literal: Yikun, styled Yuanbing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikun, courtesy name Yuanbing.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twentieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Wanli 20 (1592).

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 歷考功郎中，佐侍郎楊時喬典京察，盡斥執政私人。

translations.literal: He passed through director of the Evaluations Bureau, assisting Vice Minister Yang Shiqiao in conducting the capital evaluation; he fully dismissed the ruling faction's private clients.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Director of the Evaluations Bureau, he assisted Vice Minister Yang Shiqiao in the capital evaluation and expelled every protege of the ruling faction.

sentences.zh: 已，改文選，遷太常少卿，以憂去。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was transferred to Appointments, promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and departed on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved to the Appointments Bureau, rose to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 久之，由故官擢右僉都御史，巡撫浙江。

translations.literal: After a long while, from his former office he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官曹奉建鎮海寺於普陀山。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched eunuch Cao Feng to build Zhenhai Temple on Mount Putuo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Cao Feng to build Zhenhai Temple on Mount Putuo.

sentences.zh: 一焜偕巡按李邦華爭不可，不聽。

translations.literal: Yikun together with touring inspector Li Banghua protested that it could not be done; [the emperor] would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikun and Touring Inspector Li Banghua protested vigorously, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 織造中官劉成卒，一焜屢疏請勿遣代。

translations.literal: Weaving eunuch Liu Cheng died; Yikun repeatedly submitted memorials asking that no replacement be sent.
translations.idiomatic: When the weaving eunuch Liu Cheng died, Liu Yikun repeatedly memorialized asking that no successor be sent.

sentences.zh: 已得請，會命中官呂貴護成遺裝，奸人遂請留貴督織造，疏直達禁中。

translations.literal: He had already obtained assent when an order commanded eunuch Lü Gui to escort Cheng's leftover effects; schemers then requested that Gui be kept to supervise weaving; the memorial went straight to the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: He had just won the argument when the emperor ordered the eunuch Lü Gui to collect Liu Cheng's effects. Schemers then petitioned to keep Lü Gui as weaving supervisor, and the memorial went straight to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 一焜與邦華極論其罪，帝卒命貴代之。

translations.literal: Yikun and Banghua argued to the utmost against his crimes; the emperor in the end ordered Gui to replace [Cheng].
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikun and Li Banghua denounced the scheme in the strongest terms, but the emperor ultimately ordered Lü Gui to take over.

sentences.zh: 一焜復疏爭，不報。

translations.literal: Yikun again submitted a memorial arguing; no reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikun memorialized again in protest but received no response.

sentences.zh: 貴既任，條行十事，多侵擾。

translations.literal: Once Gui took office, he listed and implemented ten items; most were invasive harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office Lü Gui issued ten directives, most of them intrusive and disruptive.

sentences.zh: 一焜疏駁，且禁治其爪牙，貴為斂威。

translations.literal: Yikun submitted a memorial of rebuttal and also forbade and punished his minions; Gui thereby restrained his might.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikun rebutted them in memorial and moved to suppress his agents, forcing Lü Gui to curb his excesses.

sentences.zh: 一焜以暇築龕山海塘千二百丈，浚復餘杭南湖，民賴其利。

translations.literal: In his spare time Yikun built the Kan Mountain sea wall for twelve hundred zhang and dredged and restored South Lake in Yuhang; the people relied on their benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In quieter moments Liu Yikun built twelve hundred zhang of sea wall at Kan Mountain and dredged the South Lake in Yuhang, works on which the people came to depend.

sentences.zh: 御史沈珣誣訐其贓私，一焜自引去。

translations.literal: Censor Shen Xun slanderously accused him of graft and private wrongs; Yikun withdrew of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Shen Xun falsely accused him of corruption, Liu Yikun resigned on his own initiative.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Upon death, Right Vice Minister of Works was posthumously conferred.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 一煜，兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Yiyu, bureau director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yiyu served as a bureau director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 韓爌，字象雲，蒲州人。

translations.literal: Han Kuang, styled Xiangyun, a man of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang, courtesy name Xiangyun, was a native of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twentieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Wanli 20 (1592).

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 進編修，歷少詹事，充東宮講官。

translations.literal: He advanced to compiler, passed through junior tutor, and served as Eastern Palace lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to compiler, served as junior tutor, and was appointed lecturer to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，擢禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites on the right and assisted in managing the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 45 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 久之，命教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was ordered to instruct the Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed to instruct the Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年正月，兩人以帝為皇孫時，未嘗出閣讀書，請於十二日即開經筵，自後日講不輟，從之。

translations.literal: In the first month of Tianqi 1, the two men, [noting that] when the emperor had been imperial grandson he had never left the side hall to study, requested that on the twelfth day the classics lecture be opened at once and thereafter daily lecturing not cease; [the emperor] assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianqi 1, noting that the emperor had never received formal schooling as imperial grandson, the two asked that the classics lecture begin on the twelfth and continue daily without interruption. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遼陽失，都城震驚。

translations.literal: Liaoyang was lost; the capital city was shaken in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaoyang fell, the capital was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 爌、一燝以人情偷玩，擬御劄戒勵百官，共圖實效，帝納之。

translations.literal: Kuang and Yijing, [holding that] human sentiment was lax and playful, drafted an imperial letter to admonish and encourage the hundred officials to jointly seek practical results; the emperor adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang and Liu Yijing, alarmed at the prevailing laxity, drafted an imperial message urging every official to pursue real results. The emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 廷臣以兵餉大絀，合詞請發帑，爌、一燝亦以為言，詔發百萬兩。

translations.literal: Court ministers, because military supplies were greatly short, jointly petitioned to disburse the treasury; Kuang and Yijing also spoke to this; an edict issued one million taels.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials, citing severe shortfalls in military funds, petitioned together for treasury disbursement. Han Kuang and Liu Yijing supported them, and an edict released one million taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 大婚禮成，加少保、吏部尚書、武英殿大學士，蔭一子尚寶司丞。

translations.literal: When the grand marriage rite was completed, he was promoted to Junior Guardian, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Eminence; one son was ennobled as vice director of the Imperial Credentials Office.
translations.idiomatic: After the grand wedding ceremony he was promoted to Junior Guardian, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Eminence, and one son received a hereditary appointment as vice director of the Imperial Credentials Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以貴州平苗功，加少傅、太子太傅、建極殿大學士。

translations.literal: Before long, on merit of pacifying the Miao in Guizhou, he was promoted to Junior Tutor, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Establishing the Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, rewarded for pacifying the Miao in Guizhou, he was made Junior Tutor, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Establishing the Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 帝封乳母客氏為奉聖夫人，大婚成，當出外，仍留之宮中。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed wet nurse Ke Shi as Lady of Consecrated Sage; when the grand marriage was completed she ought to have gone out, yet she was still kept in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ennobled his wet nurse Ke Shi as Lady of Consecrated Sage. After the grand wedding she should have left the palace, yet he kept her within.

sentences.zh: 御史畢佐周切諫，六科、十三道復連署爭，皆不納。

translations.literal: Censor Bi Zuozhou remonstrated sharply; the Six Offices and Thirteen Circuits again jointly signed in contention; none was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Bi Zuozhou remonstrated forcefully. The Six Offices and Thirteen Circuits submitted a joint petition in protest. The emperor rejected them all.

sentences.zh: 爌、一燝引祖制為言，乃命俟梓宮發引，擇日出宮。

translations.literal: Kuang and Yijing cited ancestral institutions; thereupon he was ordered to wait until the deceased emperor's coffin departed on procession, then choose a day to leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang and Liu Yijing cited ancestral precedent, and the emperor agreed to send Ke Shi out only after the late emperor's coffin had departed, on a chosen day.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，禮部尚書孫慎行劾方從哲用李可灼紅丸藥，罪同弒逆，廷議紛然。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, Minister of Rites Sun Shenxing impeached Fang Congzhe for employing Li Kezhuo's red-pill medicine, the crime equal to regicide; court debate was clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianqi 2, Rites Minister Sun Shenxing impeached Fang Congzhe for administering Li Kezhuo's red pill, a crime he equated with regicide. Court opinion erupted into furious debate.

sentences.zh: 一燝已去位，爌特疏白其事，曰：

translations.literal: Yijing had already left office; Kuang specially submitted a memorial to clarify the matter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing had already left office. Han Kuang submitted a special memorial to set the record straight, stating:

sentences.zh: 先帝以去年八月朔踐阼。

translations.literal: The late emperor ascended the throne on the first day of the eighth month of last year.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor took the throne on the first day of the eighth month of the previous year.

sentences.zh: 臣及一燝以二十四日入閣。

translations.literal: I and Yijing entered the Grand Secretariat on the twenty-fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing and I entered the Grand Secretariat on the twenty-fourth.

sentences.zh: 適鴻臚寺官李可灼云有仙丹欲進。

translations.literal: Just then Honglu Temple official Li Kezhuo said he had an elixir and wished to present it.
translations.idiomatic: At that very time Honglu Temple official Li Kezhuo announced that he had an elixir to present.

sentences.zh: 從哲愕然，出所具問安揭，有「進藥十分宜慎」語。

translations.literal: Congzhe was startled and produced the health inquiry note he had prepared, containing the phrase "presenting medicine— utmost caution is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Congzhe was startled and produced the health-inquiry note he had prepared, which contained the words, "Medicine must be administered with the utmost caution."

sentences.zh: 臣等深以為然，即諭之去。

translations.literal: We deeply held this correct and immediately instructed him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: We fully agreed and told him to leave at once.

sentences.zh: 二十七日召見群臣，先帝自言不用藥已二十餘日。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh the late emperor summoned and saw the ministers; he himself said he had not used medicine for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh the late emperor received the ministers and said he had gone without medicine for more than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 至二十九日遇兩內臣，言帝疾已大漸，有鴻臚寺官李可灼來思善門進藥。

translations.literal: By the twenty-ninth we encountered two inner servants who said the emperor's illness had greatly worsened, and that Honglu Temple official Li Kezhuo had come to the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness to present medicine.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth we met two palace eunuchs who reported that the emperor's illness had taken a grave turn and that Honglu Temple official Li Kezhuo had come to the Gate of Reflecting on Goodness to offer medicine.

sentences.zh: 從哲及臣等皆言彼稱仙丹，便不敢信。

translations.literal: Congzhe and we all said that since he called it an elixir, we dared not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Congzhe and the rest of us all replied that because he called it an elixir, we could not trust it.

sentences.zh: 是日仍召見。

translations.literal: That day he still summoned and received audience.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor received us again.

sentences.zh: 諸臣問安畢，先帝即顧皇上，命臣等輔佐為堯、舜。

translations.literal: After the ministers finished inquiring after his health, the late emperor at once looked toward the emperor and commanded us to assist him to become Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: After we had paid our respects, the late emperor turned to the heir and charged us to help him become a ruler worthy of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 又語及壽宮，臣等以先帝山陵封，則云：「是朕壽宮。」

translations.literal: He also spoke of the longevity palace; we, [saying] the late emperor's tomb mountain was sealed, then he said: "That is my longevity palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of his tomb. When we noted that construction of the imperial mausoleum had been sealed off, he said, "That is my longevity palace.

sentences.zh: 因問有鴻臚官進藥。

translations.literal: He then asked whether there was a Honglu official presenting medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked whether a Honglu official had come to offer medicine.

sentences.zh: 從哲奏云：「李可灼自謂仙丹，臣等未敢信。」

translations.literal: Congzhe memorialized saying: "Li Kezhuo calls it an elixir himself; we have not dared believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Congzhe reported: "Li Kezhuo himself claims it is an elixir; we have not dared to trust it.

sentences.zh: 先帝即命傳宣。

translations.literal: The late emperor immediately commanded it be announced and transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor immediately ordered Li Kezhuo summoned.

sentences.zh: 臣等出，移時可灼至，同入診視，言病源及治法甚合。

translations.literal: We withdrew; after a while Kezhuo arrived; together we entered to examine and view; he spoke of the illness's source and treatment method very fittingly.
translations.idiomatic: We withdrew; shortly afterward Li Kezhuo arrived and we entered together to examine the emperor. His diagnosis and proposed treatment seemed entirely apt.

sentences.zh: 先帝喜，命速進。

translations.literal: The late emperor rejoiced and ordered it be quickly presented.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was pleased and ordered the medicine brought at once.

sentences.zh: 臣等復出，令與諸醫商榷。

translations.literal: We again went out and ordered him to consult with the various physicians.
translations.idiomatic: We withdrew again and told Li Kezhuo to consult with the attending physicians.

sentences.zh: 一燝語臣，其鄉兩人用此，損益參半。

translations.literal: Yijing told me that two men of his home district had used this; benefit and harm were half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing told me that two men from his home district had taken this medicine with mixed results— some benefited, some were harmed.

sentences.zh: 諸臣相視，實未敢明言宜否。

translations.literal: The ministers looked at one another; truly none dared to speak clearly whether it was suitable or not.
translations.idiomatic: We looked at one another; none of us dared openly say whether the medicine should be given.

sentences.zh: 須臾，先帝趨和藥，臣等復同入。

translations.literal: In a moment the late emperor urged the medicine be mixed; we again entered together.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor pressed for the medicine to be prepared, and we entered again together.

sentences.zh: 可灼調以進，先帝喜曰：「忠臣，忠臣。」

translations.literal: Kezhuo compounded and presented it; the late emperor rejoiced and said: "Loyal minister, loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kezhuo prepared and administered the dose. The late emperor exclaimed with pleasure, "A loyal subject— a loyal subject!

sentences.zh: 臣等出，少頃，中使傳聖體服藥後暖潤舒暢，思進飲膳，諸臣歡躍而退。

translations.literal: We withdrew; shortly after, an inner messenger transmitted that the sacred person after taking medicine was warm, moist, smooth, and comfortable, and wished to take food and drink; the ministers joyfully leapt and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: We withdrew. Soon a palace messenger reported that after taking the medicine the emperor felt warm, comfortable, and at ease, and wished to eat. Overjoyed, we withdrew.

sentences.zh: 比申末，可灼出云：「聖上恐藥力不繼，欲再進一丸。」

translations.literal: By the end of the Shen hour Kezhuo came out saying: "The sacred sovereign fears the medicinal power will not continue and wishes to take another pill.
translations.idiomatic: Near dusk Li Kezhuo came out and said, "His Majesty fears the medicine's effect will fade and wishes to take another pill.

sentences.zh: 諸醫言不宜驟。

translations.literal: The various physicians said it was not suitable to do so abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: The physicians said another dose would be inadvisable so soon.

sentences.zh: 乃傳趨益急，因再進訖。

translations.literal: Then the transmission urged ever more urgently; thereby a second presentation was completed.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor's summons grew ever more urgent, and a second dose was administered.

sentences.zh: 臣等問再服復何狀，答言平善如初。

translations.literal: We asked how he was after taking it again; the answer said calm and good as at first.
translations.idiomatic: We asked how the emperor was after the second dose and were told he was as calm and well as before.

sentences.zh: 此本日情事也。

translations.literal: These were the circumstances of that day.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the course of events that day.

sentences.zh: 次日，臣等趨朝，而先帝已於卯刻上賓矣，痛哉！

translations.literal: The next day we hurried to court, but the late emperor had already become a guest on high at the mao hour— how painful!
translations.idiomatic: The next morning we hurried to court, only to learn that the late emperor had passed away at dawn. Alas!

sentences.zh: 方先帝召見群臣時，被袞憑幾，儼然顧命。

translations.literal: Just when the late emperor summoned and saw the ministers, clad in imperial robes and leaning on the armrest, he seemed fully in the form of a deathbed charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor last received us, robed in imperial garments and propped on his couch, he looked for all the world like a ruler delivering his final charge.

sentences.zh: 皇上焦顏侍側，臣等環跪仿徨，操藥而前，籲天以禱。

translations.literal: The emperor with troubled countenance attended at his side; we ministers knelt all around in distraction, grasping medicine and advancing, crying to Heaven in prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The heir stood at his side, face drawn with grief. We ministers knelt in anguish around them, bringing medicine forward and praying to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣子際此，憾不身代。

translations.literal: Ministers encountering this regretted they could not substitute their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Faced with such a moment, every minister would have gladly traded his own life for the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 凡今所謂宜慎宜止者，豈不慮於心，實未出於口，抑且不以萌諸心。

translations.literal: All that is now called "ought to be cautious, ought to be stopped"— was it not considered in the heart? Truly it had not come from the mouth, and moreover had not even been conceived in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: As for the cautions and objections now being spoken of— we had never voiced them, had never even entertained them in our hearts.

sentences.zh: 念先帝臨御雖止旬月，恩膏實被九垓。

translations.literal: Reflecting that though the late emperor held rule for only ten-odd months, his grace truly covered the nine regions.
translations.idiomatic: Though the late emperor reigned scarcely ten months, his grace had reached every corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 為臣子者宜何如頌揚，何如紀述。

translations.literal: As ministers and subjects, how ought one praise and extol, how ought one record and recount?
translations.idiomatic: What tribute, what record, could a loyal subject offer such a ruler?

sentences.zh: 乃禮臣忠憤之激談，與遠邇驚疑之紛議，不知謂當時若何情景，而進藥始末實止如此。

translations.literal: Yet the rites ministers' loyal indignant heated talk and the near and far startled doubtful clamorous debate— one does not know what they suppose the scene was then; the beginning and end of presenting medicine in truth stopped at just this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rites officials speak in loyal outrage, and near and far the court buzzes with suspicion— as though they imagine some scene we never witnessed. The truth of the medicine affair was exactly as I have described.

sentences.zh: 若不據實詳剖，直舉非命之兇稱，加諸考終之令主，恐先帝在天之靈不無恫怨，皇上終天之念何以為懷。

translations.literal: If one does not slice open and examine in detail according to fact, but directly lifts the murderous name of untimely death and adds it upon the order-giving lord who ended in due course— I fear the late emperor's spirit in Heaven would not be without startled resentment; how would the emperor's lifelong remembrance find its place in the heart?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not examine the facts but instead brand our virtuous late sovereign with the charge of violent death, I fear his spirit in Heaven would be aggrieved beyond measure, and how could the emperor bear such eternal grief?

sentences.zh: 乞渙發綸音，布告中外，俾議法者勿以小疑成大疑，編摹者勿以信史為謗史。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be swiftly issued and proclaimed within and without, so that those deliberating the law may not make a small doubt into a great doubt, and those compiling and copying may not take credible history as slander-history.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue an edict at once, proclaiming the truth throughout the realm, so that those who judge the case may not magnify a small doubt into a grave one, and historians may not turn faithful record into libel.

sentences.zh: 文震孟建言獲譴，論救甚力。

translations.literal: Wen Zhenmeng submitted advice and received censure; [Kuang] argued to save him very forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Zhenmeng was punished for his memorial, Han Kuang fought strenuously for his reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 三年，以山東平妖賊功，加少師、太子太師。

translations.literal: In the third year, on merit of pacifying demonic bandits in Shandong, he was promoted to Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 3, rewarded for suppressing rebel bandits in Shandong, he was made Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時葉向高當國，爌次之。

translations.literal: At that time Ye Xianggao held the state; Kuang was second to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao was then directing affairs of state, with Han Kuang as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 及楊漣劾魏忠賢二十四大罪，忠賢頗懼，求援於爌。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian on twenty-four great crimes, Zhongxian was quite fearful and sought aid from Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian on twenty-four capital crimes, Zhongxian grew alarmed and turned to Han Kuang for help.

sentences.zh: 爌不應，忠賢深銜之。

translations.literal: Kuang did not respond; Zhongxian deeply harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang refused him, and Wei Zhongxian never forgave the snub.

sentences.zh: 既向高罷，爌為首輔，每事持正，為善類所倚。

translations.literal: Once Xianggao was dismissed, Kuang became chief grand secretary; in every matter he held to the upright, and was relied upon by the upright faction.
translations.idiomatic: After Ye Xianggao left office, Han Kuang became chief grand secretary. He stood firm on principle in every affair, and men of integrity looked to him for leadership.

sentences.zh: 然向高有智術，籠絡群奄，爌惟廉直自持，勢不能敵。

translations.literal: Yet Xianggao had craft and stratagem, and co-opted the eunuch clique; Kuang could only maintain himself by integrity and uprightness, and in power could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao, however, had been shrewd enough to win over the eunuchs. Han Kuang relied on nothing but personal integrity, and could not hold his ground against such forces.

sentences.zh: 而同官魏廣微又深結忠賢，遍引邪黨。

translations.literal: Moreover his colleague Wei Guangwei deeply allied with Zhongxian and broadly brought in the corrupt faction.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile his colleague Wei Guangwei had forged close ties with Wei Zhongxian and was filling the court with allies from the corrupt faction.

sentences.zh: 其冬，忠賢假會推事逐趙南星、高攀龍，爌急率朱國禎等上言：「陛下一日去兩大臣，臣民失望。

translations.literal: That winter, Zhongxian used the matter of collective nomination to drive out Zhao Nanxing and Gao Panlong; Kuang urgently led Zhu Guozhen and others in memorializing: 'Your Majesty, in a single day you have removed two great ministers; officials and people are disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wei Zhongxian used the collective nomination process as a pretext to purge Zhao Nanxing and Gao Panlong. Han Kuang hastily led Zhu Guozhen and others in a memorial: 'Your Majesty has dismissed two senior ministers in a single day. The court and the people have lost heart.

sentences.zh: 且中旨徑宣，不復到閣，而攀龍一疏，經臣等擬上者，又復更易，大駭聽聞，有傷國體。」

translations.literal: Moreover imperial edicts were proclaimed directly and no longer came to the Grand Secretariat; and a memorial of Panlong that had been drafted by us ministers for submission was again altered—greatly shocking those who heard it, and injuring the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, palace edicts were now issued directly, bypassing the Grand Secretariat altogether. A memorial from Gao Panlong that we had drafted for submission was altered again. The news shocked everyone who heard it and damaged the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 忠賢益不悅，傳旨切責。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was all the more displeased and transmitted an edict sharply rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was further enraged and had an edict issued sharply rebuking them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又逐楊漣、左光斗、陳於廷，朝政大變，忠賢勢益張。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, and Chen Yuting were also driven out; court governance changed greatly, and Zhongxian's power grew ever more expansive.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, and Chen Yuting were driven out as well. Court politics turned sharply, and Wei Zhongxian's power swelled.

sentences.zh: 故事，閣中秉筆止首輔一人。

translations.literal: By precedent, within the Grand Secretariat only the chief grand secretary wielded the brush.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, only the chief grand secretary held the brush in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 廣微欲分其柄，囑忠賢傳旨，諭爌同寅協恭，而責次輔毋伴食。

translations.literal: Guangwei wished to divide that authority; he instructed Zhongxian to transmit an edict telling Kuang's colleagues to cooperate harmoniously, while rebuking the second grand secretary for merely eating alongside without working.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangwei wanted a share of that authority. He had Wei Zhongxian issue an edict instructing Han Kuang's colleagues to cooperate harmoniously, while rebuking the second grand secretary for holding office without doing the work.

sentences.zh: 爌惶懼，即抗疏乞休。

translations.literal: Kuang was fearful and alarmed, and immediately submitted a defiant memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang, alarmed, immediately submitted a forthright memorial asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 略言：「臣備位綸扉，咎愆日積。

translations.literal: He stated in summary: 'I occupy a place in the Grand Secretariat, and my faults and transgressions accumulate day by day.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in summary: 'I hold a place in the Grand Secretariat, yet my faults mount by the day.

sentences.zh: 如詰戎宜先營衛，而觀兵禁掖，無能紓宵旰憂。

translations.literal: For example, when discussing military affairs one should first address camp defenses, yet troops were reviewed in the forbidden inner precinct—I could not relieve the sovereign's early-morning and late-night anxieties.
translations.idiomatic: When military affairs were discussed, camp defenses should have come first—yet troops were reviewed inside the palace precincts, and I could not ease Your Majesty's ceaseless worries.

sentences.zh: 忠直尚稽召還，而榜掠朝堂，無能回震霆怒。

translations.literal: Loyal and upright men still awaited recall, yet flogging took place in the court hall—I could not turn back thunderous wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and upright men still had not been recalled, while floggings were carried out in the hall of audience, and I could not turn aside Your Majesty's thunderous anger.

sentences.zh: 後先諸臣之罷斥，諭旨中出之紛更，不能先時深念，有調劑之方，又不能臨事執持，為封還之戇。

translations.literal: The dismissals of ministers one after another, and the repeated changes in edicts issued from the palace—I could not think deeply beforehand and devise measures of adjustment; nor when matters arose could I hold firm and make the bold act of returning a memorial sealed.
translations.idiomatic: The successive dismissals of ministers, the edicts issued from the palace that kept changing—I could neither foresee them and find a way to mediate, nor when the moment came hold firm and return a memorial unapproved.

sentences.zh: 皆臣罪之大者。

translations.literal: All these are among my greatest crimes.
translations.idiomatic: These are my gravest failures.

sentences.zh: 皇上釋此不問，責臣以協恭，責同官以協贊。

translations.literal: Your Majesty releases these without inquiry, yet charges me with harmonious cooperation and charges my colleagues with cooperative assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty overlooks these failures, yet demands that I cooperate harmoniously and that my colleagues assist one another.

sentences.zh: 同官奉詔以從事，臣欲補過無由矣。

translations.literal: My colleagues receive the edict and proceed accordingly; I have no means by which to make amends for my faults.
translations.idiomatic: My colleagues will obey the edict and act accordingly. I have no way left to redeem my failures.

sentences.zh: 乞亟褫臣官，為佐理溺職之戒。」

translations.literal: I beg that my office be swiftly stripped away, as a warning to those who assist in governance yet fail in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that my office be taken from me at once, as a warning to those who share in governance yet neglect their duties.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「卿親承顧命，當竭忠盡職。

translations.literal: The reply came: 'You personally received the deathbed charge; you ought to exhaust loyalty and fulfill your duties.
translations.idiomatic: The reply came: 'You personally received the late emperor's deathbed charge. You should serve with full loyalty and diligence.

sentences.zh: 乃歸非於上，退有後言。

translations.literal: Yet you shift blame to your sovereign, and after withdrawing have further complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Instead you shift blame upward, and even after withdrawing you keep airing grievances.

sentences.zh: 今復悻悻求去，可馳驛還籍。」

translations.literal: Now you again resentfully seek to leave; you may take courier horses and return to your native place.'
translations.idiomatic: Now you resentfully seek to leave again. Take the courier relay and return to your native place.'

sentences.zh: 諸輔臣請如故事，加以體貌，不報。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries requested that, according to precedent, ceremonial honors be granted him; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries asked that he be granted the customary ceremonial honors on departure, as precedent required. No answer came.

sentences.zh: 爌疏謝，有「左右前後務近端良，重綸綍以重仕途，肅紀綱以肅朝寧」語。

translations.literal: Kuang submitted a memorial of thanks containing the words: 'Those before and behind, to left and right, must strive to keep upright and good men near; give weight to imperial rescripts to give weight to the official path; discipline regulations to secure court tranquility.'
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang submitted a farewell memorial containing the words: 'Those around the throne must keep upright men close; give weight to imperial rescripts so that office carries weight; enforce discipline so that the court may know peace.'

sentences.zh: 忠賢及其黨益恨。

translations.literal: Zhongxian and his faction hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian and his allies hated him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 爌去，朱國禎為首輔。

translations.literal: When Kuang departed, Zhu Guozhen became chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Kuang left, Zhu Guozhen became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 李蕃攻去之，顧秉謙代其位。

translations.literal: Li Fan attacked and drove him out; Gu Bingqian replaced him in that position.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan attacked him until he was removed, and Gu Bingqian took his place.

sentences.zh: 公卿庶僚，皆忠賢私人矣。

translations.literal: Grand ministers and the multitude of officials were all Zhongxian's private men.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers high and low were now Wei Zhongxian's own men.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，逆黨李魯生劾爌，削籍除名。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, the traitor-faction member Li Lusheng impeached Kuang; he was stricken from the registry and removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of the Tianqi reign, Li Lusheng of the eunuch faction impeached Han Kuang, who was stricken from the rolls and expelled from office.

sentences.zh: 又假他事坐贓二千，斃其家人於獄。

translations.literal: On a pretext of another matter he was convicted of two thousand taels in corrupt gains, and his family members were beaten to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: On another pretext he was convicted of embezzling two thousand taels, and members of his household were beaten to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 爌鬻田宅，貸親故以償，乃棲止先墓上。

translations.literal: Kuang sold fields and houses, borrowed from relatives and friends to pay the debt, and then took shelter at his ancestral tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang sold his land and house, borrowed from relatives and friends to pay the fine, and took shelter beside his family's ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝登極，復故官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie ascended the throne, Kuang's former office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chongzhen took the throne, Han Kuang's former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，言者爭請召用，為逆黨楊維垣等所扼，但賜敕存問，官其一子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, memorialists competed in requesting his recall to office; he was blocked by traitor-faction men such as Yang Weiyuan, and only received an imperial letter of inquiry and an appointment for one son.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen, officials clamored for his recall, but Yang Weiyuan and others of the old eunuch faction blocked it. The emperor sent only a letter of inquiry and granted an office to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 至五月，始遣行人召之。

translations.literal: Only in the fifth month was a palace messenger dispatched to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the fifth month was a palace messenger sent to summon him back.

sentences.zh: 十二月還朝，復為首輔。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he returned to court and again became chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court in the twelfth month and again became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝御文華後殿閱章奏，召爌等，諭以擬旨務消異同，開誠和衷，期於至當。

translations.literal: The emperor presided in the rear hall of Wenhua to review memorials, summoned Kuang and the others, and instructed them that in drafting rescripts they must eliminate differences, open sincerity and harmony of purpose, and aim at what is most fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reviewed memorials in the rear hall of Wenhua Palace, summoned Han Kuang and the others, and instructed them that when drafting rescripts they should settle disagreements, speak openly and in good faith, and aim at what was truly right.

sentences.zh: 爌等頓首謝，退言：「上所諭甚善，而密勿政機，諸臣參互擬議，不必顯言分合。

translations.literal: Kuang and the others bowed their heads in thanks; upon withdrawing they said: 'What Your Majesty instructed is very good; yet in the confidential affairs of state, when ministers jointly deliberate and draft, there is no need to speak openly of division and union.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang and the others kowtowed in thanks. On withdrawing they said: 'Your Majesty's instruction is excellent. Yet in the confidential business of state, when ministers deliberate together, there is no need to speak openly of who agrees and who does not.

sentences.zh: 至臣等晨夕入直，勢不能報謝賓客。

translations.literal: As for us ministers entering duty morning and evening, we cannot in the circumstances receive and thank guests.
translations.idiomatic: As for us, we attend duty morning and evening and cannot in that time receive and entertain visitors as courtesy requires.

sentences.zh: 商政事者，宜相見於朝房，而一切禁私邸交際。」

translations.literal: Those who wish to discuss state affairs ought to meet in the court rooms, and all private-residence socializing should be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to discuss state affairs should meet in the court rooms, and all social calls at private residences should be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 帝即諭百僚遵行。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately instructed all officials to obey and carry this out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered the entire bureaucracy to comply.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，大學士劉鴻訓以張慶臻敕書事被重譴，爌疏救，不聽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun was heavily punished over the matter of Zhang Qingzhen's commission letter; Kuang memorialized to save him, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun was severely punished over Zhang Qingzhen's commission letter. Han Kuang memorialized in his defense, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁訐錢謙益，御史任贊化亦疏訐體仁。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren impeached Qian Qianyi, and Censor Ren Zanhua also memorialized impeaching Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren attacked Qian Qianyi, and Censor Ren Zanhua memorialized attacking Wen Tiren in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝召見廷臣，體仁力詆贊化及御史毛羽健為謙益死黨。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned court ministers for audience; Tiren forcefully denounced Zanhua and Censor Mao Yujian as diehard partisans of Qianyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the court. Wen Tiren fiercely denounced Ren Zanhua and Censor Mao Yujian as Qian Qianyi's diehard partisans.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責贊化。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sharply rebuked Zanhua.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and sharply rebuked Ren Zanhua.

sentences.zh: 爌請寬贊化以安體仁。

translations.literal: Kuang requested leniency for Zanhua in order to reassure Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang asked that Ren Zanhua be treated leniently so as to reassure Wen Tiren.

sentences.zh: 帝因謂：「進言者不憂國而植黨，自名東林，於朝事何補？」

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon said: 'Those who offer advice do not worry for the state but plant factions; they call themselves Donglin—what help is that to court affairs?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said: 'Those who speak up do not worry for the state but build factions. They call themselves Donglin—what good does that do the court?

sentences.zh: 爌退，具揭言：「人臣不可以黨事君，人君亦不可以黨疑臣。

translations.literal: Kuang withdrew and submitted a detailed memorial stating: 'Ministers must not serve their sovereign through faction; nor may the sovereign suspect ministers through faction.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang withdrew and submitted a detailed memorial: 'Ministers must not serve their sovereign through faction, and a sovereign must not judge his ministers through faction.

sentences.zh: 但當論其才品臧否，職業修廢，而黜陟之。

translations.literal: One should only judge their talent and character, good or bad, and whether their duties are well or poorly performed, and promote or demote accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: They should be judged only on talent and character, on whether their work is sound or neglected, and promoted or dismissed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 若戈矛妄起於朝堂，畛域橫分於宮府，非國之福也。」

translations.literal: If spears and shields rise recklessly in the court hall, and boundaries are drawn across palace and government, that is not a blessing to the state.'
translations.idiomatic: If spears are raised recklessly in the hall of audience and the palace and the ministries are carved into hostile camps, that is no blessing for the state.'

sentences.zh: 又率同官力救贊化，不納。

translations.literal: He again led his colleagues in strenuously pleading for Zanhua; the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: He again led his colleagues in a strenuous plea for Ren Zanhua, but the emperor would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 皇長子生，請盡蠲天下積逋，報可。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was born, he requested that all accumulated tax arrears nationwide be fully remitted; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was born, he requested a full remission of accumulated tax arrears nationwide. The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 時大治忠賢黨，爌與李標、錢龍錫主之。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei Zhongxian faction was being thoroughly prosecuted; Kuang, together with Li Biao and Qian Longxi, directed it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was conducting a major purge of Wei Zhongxian's faction, led by Han Kuang, Li Biao, and Qian Longxi.

sentences.zh: 列上二百六十二人，罪分六等，名曰「欽定逆案」，頒行天下。

translations.literal: They listed 262 persons, crimes divided into six grades, named the 'Imperially Designated Treason Case,' and promulgated it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They listed 262 names, divided crimes into six grades, titled the list the 'Imperially Designated Treason Case,' and promulgated it throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 言者爭擊吏部尚書王永光，南京禮部主事王永吉言之尤力。

translations.literal: Memorialists competed in attacking Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang; Wang Yongji, a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, spoke against him with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists competed in attacking Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang. Wang Yongji, a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, spoke against him with particular force.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，將罪之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and was about to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and was about to punish Wang Yongji.

sentences.zh: 爌等言永吉不宥，永光必不安，乃止奪俸一年。

translations.literal: Kuang and the others said that if Yongji were not pardoned, Yongguang would certainly be unsettled; the punishment was therefore limited to stripping one year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang and the others argued that if Wang Yongji were not pardoned, Wang Yongguang would never settle down. The emperor relented and reduced the penalty to one year's loss of salary.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書張鳳翔奏廠、庫積弊。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Fengxiang memorialized on accumulated abuses in the factories and warehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Fengxiang memorialized on long-standing abuses in the imperial factories and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召對廷臣詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned court ministers for audience, and interrogated and rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry, summoned the court for audience, and sharply interrogated the ministers.

sentences.zh: 巡視科道王都、高賚明二人力辨，帝命錦衣官執之，爌、標、龍錫並救解。

translations.literal: The inspecting censors Wang Du and Gao Ziming argued forcefully in their defense; the emperor ordered brocade-clad guard officers to seize them; Kuang, Biao, and Longxi together pleaded for their release.
translations.idiomatic: The inspecting censors Wang Du and Gao Ziming argued their case forcefully. The emperor ordered the brocade-clad guards to seize them. Han Kuang, Li Biao, and Qian Longxi together interceded for their release.

sentences.zh: 而是日永光以羽健疏劾，請帝究主使者。

translations.literal: But that same day Yongguang, on the basis of Mao Yujian's impeachment memorial, asked the emperor to investigate who had been behind it.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, citing Mao Yujian's impeachment memorial, Wang Yongguang asked the emperor to investigate who had instigated it.

sentences.zh: 爌退，申救都等，因言永光不宜請究言官。

translations.literal: Kuang withdrew and again pleaded for Wang Du and the others, adding that Yongguang ought not to request investigation of censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang withdrew and again pleaded for Wang Du and the others, adding that Wang Yongguang should not demand an investigation of the censor who had spoken out.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，然羽健卒獲免。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it, yet Mao Yujian ultimately escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept the plea, but Mao Yujian ultimately escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 初，熊廷弼既死，傳首九邊，屍不得歸葬。

translations.literal: Initially, after Xiong Tingbi had died, his head was sent through the nine border regions as a warning, and his corpse could not be returned for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Xiong Tingbi's execution his head had been sent through the nine border regions as a warning, and his body was never allowed a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 至是，其子詣闕疏請。

translations.literal: At this time his son came to the palace gate and submitted a memorial requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: At this point his son came to the capital and submitted a memorial requesting burial.

sentences.zh: 爌等因言：「廷弼之死，由逆奄欲殺楊漣、魏大中，誣以行賄，因盡殺漣等，復懸坐廷弼贓銀十七萬，刑及妻孥，冤之甚者。」

translations.literal: Kuang and the others thereupon said: 'Tingbi's death came because the rebellious eunuchs wished to kill Yang Lian and Wei Dazhong; they falsely charged bribery, and thus killed Lian and the others entirely; they then falsely imputed upon Tingbi 170,000 taels of corrupt silver, and punishment reached his wife and children—a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang and the others wrote: 'Xiong Tingbi died because the eunuch faction wanted to destroy Yang Lian and Wei Dazhong. They framed them for bribery and killed them, then falsely imputed 170,000 taels of corrupt silver on Tingbi and punished his wife and children. The injustice was extreme.

sentences.zh: 帝乃許收葬。

translations.literal: The emperor then permitted the body to be recovered for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then granted permission for the body to be recovered and buried.

sentences.zh: 時遼事急，朝議汰各鎮兵。

translations.literal: At that time the Liaodong crisis was urgent, and the court debated reducing troops in the various garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong crisis was urgent, and the court debated cutting troops across the border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 又以兵科給事中劉懋疏，議裁驛卒。

translations.literal: Also, on the memorial of Liu Mao, supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs, they debated cutting courier-station personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On a memorial from Liu Mao, supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs, they also debated cutting personnel from the courier relay system.

sentences.zh: 帝以問爌，爌言：「汰兵止當清占冒及增設冗兵爾。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Kuang; Kuang said: 'Reducing troops should only mean clearing falsely claimed slots and redundantly added supernumerary troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Han Kuang, who replied: 'Troop reductions should target only falsely claimed slots and redundantly added supernumeraries.

sentences.zh: 沖地額兵不可汰也。

translations.literal: Front-line quota troops must not be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Front-line quota troops must not be cut.

sentences.zh: 驛傳疲累，當責按臣核減，以蘇民困，其所節省，仍還之民。」

translations.literal: The courier relay system is worn out and burdensome; investigating censors should be charged with verifying reductions to relieve the people's distress, and whatever is saved should still be returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The courier relay system has become an unbearable burden. Investigating censors should be charged with verifying reductions to relieve the people's distress, and whatever is saved should be returned to them.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 御史高捷、史褷以罪免，永光力引之。

translations.literal: Censors Gao Jie and Shi Shi had been dismissed for crimes; Yongguang strongly recommended them for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Gao Jie and Shi Shi had been dismissed for misconduct. Wang Yongguang strongly pressed for their reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 都御史曹於汴持不可，永光再疏爭。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Cao Yubian held that it could not be done; Yongguang memorialized again in dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Cao Yubian objected. Wang Yongguang memorialized again in protest.

sentences.zh: 爌言，故事當聽都察院咨用。

translations.literal: Kuang said that by precedent the Censorate's recommendation for appointment should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang said that by precedent such appointments required the Censorate's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 帝方眷永光，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor was then favoring Yongguang and did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then favoring Wang Yongguang and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 九月，以將行慶典，請停秋決，亦不從。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because a celebratory rite was about to be held, he requested suspension of the autumn executions; this too was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, with a celebratory rite approaching, he asked that autumn executions be suspended. That request was also rejected.

sentences.zh: 時逆案雖定，永光及袁弘勛、捷、褷輩日為翻案計。

translations.literal: Although the treason case had been settled, Yongguang together with Yuan Hongxun, Jie, Shi, and their like daily plotted to reverse the verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: Although the treason case had been settled, Wang Yongguang, Yuan Hongxun, Gao Jie, Shi Shi, and their allies were daily scheming to reverse the verdicts.

sentences.zh: 至十月，大清兵入畿甸，都城戒嚴。

translations.literal: By the tenth month the Great Qing army entered the capital region, and the capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth month Qing forces had entered the capital region, and Beijing was placed under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 初，袁崇煥入朝，嘗與錢龍錫語邊事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan Chonghuan came to court, he had once discussed border affairs with Qian Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yuan Chonghuan came to court, he had discussed border affairs with Qian Longxi.

sentences.zh: 龍錫，東林黨魁也，永光等謀因崇煥興大獄，可盡傾東林。

translations.literal: Longxi was a leader of the Donglin faction; Yongguang and the others plotted to use Chonghuan to launch a great case by which the Donglin could be entirely overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Longxi was a leader of the Donglin faction. Wang Yongguang and his allies plotted to use Yuan Chonghuan to launch a major prosecution that would bring down the entire Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 倡言大清兵之入，由崇煥殺毛文龍所致。

translations.literal: They spread the claim that the Great Qing army's entry came about because Chonghuan had killed Mao Wenlong.
translations.idiomatic: They spread the claim that the Qing invasion had come about because Yuan Chonghuan had executed Mao Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 捷遂首攻龍錫，逐之。

translations.literal: Jie then took the lead in attacking Longxi and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie then led the attack on Qian Longxi and drove him from office.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，中書舍人加尚寶卿原抱奇故由輸貲進，亦劾爌主款誤國，招寇欺君，郡邑殘破，宗社阽危，不能設一策，拔一人，坐視成敗，以人國僥幸，宜與龍錫並斥。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Yuan Baoqi—formerly a secretarial receptionist promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Stud, who had advanced by paying money—also impeached Kuang for advocating appeasement and ruining the state, inviting the enemy and deceiving the sovereign; counties and districts lay ravaged, the altars of state were on the brink of collapse; he could devise no single plan, raise up no single man, sat watching success and failure, gambling with the fate of the nation—he ought to be expelled together with Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Yuan Baoqi—a secretarial receptionist who had bought his way to Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Stud—also impeached Han Kuang for advocating appeasement and ruining the state, for inviting the enemy and deceiving the sovereign. Counties lay in ruins, the dynasty stood on the brink of collapse, yet he had offered no plan, raised up no man, and merely watched fortune turn while gambling with the nation's fate. He ought to be expelled together with Qian Longxi.

sentences.zh: 其言主款者，以爌，崇煥座主也。

translations.literal: The reason for saying he advocated appeasement was that Kuang was Chonghuan's chief examiner.
translations.idiomatic: The charge of advocating appeasement rested on the fact that Han Kuang had been Yuan Chonghuan's chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 帝重去爌，貶抱奇秩。

translations.literal: The emperor valued losing Kuang and demoted Baoqi in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reluctant to lose Han Kuang and demoted Yuan Baoqi in rank instead.

sentences.zh: 無何，左庶子丁進以遷擢愆期怨爌，亦劾之，而工部主事李逢申劾疏繼上。

translations.literal: Before long, Left Sub-Reader Ding Jin, resentful of Kuang over a delayed promotion, also impeached him; and Secretary in the Ministry of Works Li Fengshen's impeachment memorial followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Left Sub-Reader Ding Jin, resentful that Han Kuang had delayed his promotion, also impeached him. A memorial from Li Fengshen, a secretary in the Ministry of Works, followed in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 爌即三疏引疾。

translations.literal: Kuang immediately submitted three memorials citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang immediately submitted three memorials citing illness and asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔賜白金彩幣，馳驛遣行人護歸，悉如彜典。

translations.literal: An edict granted silver and silken brocade gifts, dispatched a palace messenger by courier relay to escort him home, all fully according to ceremonial precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him silver and silken brocade gifts, sent a palace messenger by courier relay to escort him home, and accorded him every customary honor on departure.

sentences.zh: 進、逢申並爌會試所舉士也。

translations.literal: Jin and Fengshen were both men Kuang had passed in the metropolitan examination.
