translations.idiomatic: Both Ding Jin and Li Fengshen were men Han Kuang had passed in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 爌先後作相，老成慎重。

translations.literal: Kuang served as chief minister on two occasions; he was mature and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang had served as chief minister twice. He was mature and cautious.

sentences.zh: 引正人，抑邪黨，天下稱其賢，獨嘗庇王永光云。

translations.literal: He brought in upright men and suppressed the corrupt faction; the realm praised his worth, though he alone once sheltered Wang Yongguang.
translations.idiomatic: He brought upright men forward and checked the corrupt faction, and the realm praised his integrity—though he had once sheltered Wang Yongguang.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，李自成陷蒲州，迫爌出見，不從。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year, Li Zicheng took Puzhou and pressed Kuang to come out and meet him; Kuang refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year Li Zicheng captured Puzhou and demanded that Han Kuang come out to meet him. He refused.

sentences.zh: 賊執其孫以脅。

translations.literal: The bandits seized his grandson to coerce him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized his grandson to coerce him.

sentences.zh: 爌止一孫，乃出見，賊釋其孫。

translations.literal: Kuang had only this one grandson; he then went out to meet them, and the bandits released his grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang had only this one grandson. He then went out to meet them, and the rebels released the boy.

sentences.zh: 爌歸，憤郁而卒，年八十矣。

translations.literal: Kuang returned home, died of indignant grief, and was eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kuang returned home and died of grief and indignation at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 朱國祚

translations.literal: Zhu Guozuo
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guozuo

sentences.zh: 朱國祚，字兆隆，秀水人。

translations.literal: Zhu Guozuo, courtesy name Zhaolong, was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guozuo, courtesy name Zhaolong, was a native of Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十一年進士第一。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he ranked first among jinshi graduates.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Wanli reign he placed first in the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 授修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed drafting compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed drafting compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 進洗馬，為皇長子侍班官，尋進諭德。

translations.literal: He was promoted to reader-in-waiting, served as attendant in the crown prince's court, and soon was promoted to preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to reader-in-waiting and served as an attendant in the crown prince's court, soon advancing to preceptor.

sentences.zh: 日本陷朝鮮，石星惑沈惟敬言，力主封貢。

translations.literal: When Japan invaded Korea, Shi Xing was beguiled by Shen Weijing's words and strongly advocated investiture and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan invaded Korea, Shi Xing was taken in by Shen Weijing and pressed hard for a policy of granting investiture and accepting tribute.

sentences.zh: 國祚面詰星：「此我鄉曲無賴，因緣為奸利耳，公獨不計辱國乎？」

translations.literal: Guozuo confronted Shi Xing face to face and interrogated him: "This fellow is a scoundrel from my hometown district who seizes opportunities for treacherous profit—do you alone not consider the humiliation of the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo confronted Shi Xing in person: "He is a local scoundrel from my home district who twists every chance for illicit gain—surely you cannot ignore the dishonor this brings upon the realm?

sentences.zh: 星不能用。

translations.literal: Shi Xing could not accept his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xing would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，超擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was unusually promoted to right vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 26 (1598) he was promoted out of turn to right vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 湖廣稅監陳奉橫甚。

translations.literal: Chen Feng, the tax superintendent in Huguang, was extremely domineering.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Feng, the Huguang tax superintendent, was flagrantly abusive in his power.

sentences.zh: 國祚貽書巡按御史曹楷，令發其狀。

translations.literal: Guozuo sent a letter to the touring censor Cao Kai, instructing him to expose Chen's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo wrote to the touring censor Cao Kai urging him to bring Chen's misconduct to light.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，幾逮楷，奉亦因此撤去。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and nearly arrested Kai; Feng was also removed on this account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and nearly had Cao Kai arrested; Chen Feng was also recalled because of the affair.

sentences.zh: 尚書余繼登卒，國祚攝部事。

translations.literal: When Minister Yu Jideng died, Guozuo acted in his stead over the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Yu Jideng died, Guozuo took charge of the ministry in his place.

sentences.zh: 時皇長子儲位未定，冠婚逾期，國祚屢疏諫。

translations.literal: At that time the heirship of the eldest imperial son was unsettled and his capping and wedding were overdue; Guozuo repeatedly memorialized to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's status was still unsettled and his coming-of-age and wedding ceremonies long overdue; Guozuo memorialized again and again in protest.

sentences.zh: 戚臣鄭國泰請先冠婚，後冊立。

translations.literal: The consort kin official Zheng Guotai requested that capping and wedding come first and investiture later.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Guotai, a kinsman of the consort, asked that the prince be capped and wed before being formally invested as heir.

sentences.zh: 國祚抗疏言：「本朝外戚不得與政事。

translations.literal: Guozuo submitted a remonstrance memorial saying: "In our dynasty consort relatives may not involve themselves in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo submitted a forceful memorial: "Consort relatives have never been permitted to meddle in government under this dynasty.

sentences.zh: 冊立大典，非國泰所宜言。

translations.literal: The great rite of investiture is not something Guotai should speak about.
translations.idiomatic: The solemn rite of investiture is no business of Guotai's to discuss.

sentences.zh: 況先冊立，後冠婚，其儀仗、冠服之制，祝醮、敕戒之辭，升降、坐立之位，朝賀拜舞之節，因名制分，因分制禮，甚嚴且辨。

translations.literal: Moreover, if investiture comes first and capping and wedding afterward, the regulations for ceremonial escorts and caps and robes, the prayers and admonitions, the positions for ascending and descending and sitting and standing, and the observances for court congratulations and bowing and dancing—all derive rank from titles and derive rites from rank—are extremely strict and clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when investiture precedes capping and wedding, the rules governing ceremonial escorts and regalia, the sacrificial prayers and admonitions, the prescribed positions for rising, sitting, and kneeling, and the choreography of court congratulations—all calibrated to rank and rank to ritual—are rigorously ordered.

sentences.zh: 一失其序，名分大乖。

translations.literal: Once the sequence is lost, titles and roles fall greatly out of accord.
translations.idiomatic: A single reversal of that order would throw rank and propriety into chaos.

sentences.zh: 違累朝祖制，背皇上明綸，犯天下清議，皆此言也。」

translations.literal: It would violate the ancestral institutions of successive reigns, run counter to Your Majesty's clear edict, and offend the sober judgment of all under Heaven—all these faults lie in this proposal."
translations.idiomatic: It would defy ancestral precedent, contradict Your Majesty's own decree, and affront public opinion nationwide—that is what this proposal amounts to.

sentences.zh: 又言：「冊立之事，理不可緩。

translations.literal: He also said: "The matter of investiture, by principle, cannot be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "The investiture can no longer be deferred on any principled grounds.

sentences.zh: 初謂小臣激聒，故遲之。

translations.literal: At first it was said that junior officials were agitating noisily, and so it was postponed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the delay was attributed to the clamor of low-ranking remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 後群臣勿言，則曰待嫡。

translations.literal: Later, when the officials were told not to speak of it, the reason given was to wait for a son of the principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was enjoined to keep silent, the excuse became waiting for a son by the empress.

sentences.zh: 及中官久無所出，則曰皇長子體弱，須其強。

translations.literal: When the palace ladies long bore no issue, the excuse was that the eldest imperial son's constitution was weak and one must wait until he grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner palace produced no heir for years, the reason shifted to the crown prince's poor health—he must first grow sturdier.

sentences.zh: 今又待兩宮落成矣。

translations.literal: Now it is said one must wait until the two palaces are completed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court must wait until the two palaces are finished.

sentences.zh: 自三殿災，朝廷大政令率御文華殿。

translations.literal: Since the fire in the three halls, major court policy has generally been handled from Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the fire that destroyed the three main halls, imperial audiences on major state business have routinely been held in Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 三禮之行，在殿不在宮。

translations.literal: The performance of the three rites lies in the hall, not in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The three ceremonies could be conducted in the hall; they need not wait on the palace.

sentences.zh: 頃歲趨辦珠寶，戶部所進，視陛下大婚數倍之。

translations.literal: In recent years pearls and jewels were hurriedly procured, and what the Ministry of Revenue submitted was several times what had been furnished for Your Majesty's own grand wedding.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls and jewels have lately been rushed into procurement at many times the scale of Your Majesty's own wedding.

sentences.zh: 遠近疑陛下借珠寶之未備，以遲典禮。

translations.literal: Near and far suspect that Your Majesty is using the unpreparedness of pearls and jewels to delay the ceremonial rites.
translations.idiomatic: People far and near suspect that the unfinished jewel collection is being used to postpone the ceremonies indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 且詔旨采辦珠寶，額二千四百萬，而天下賦稅之額乃止四百萬。

translations.literal: Moreover, the edict set the quota for procuring pearls and jewels at twenty-four million, while the empire's tax revenue quota is only four million.
translations.idiomatic: The edict called for twenty-four million taels' worth of jewels, yet the empire's total tax intake was only four million.

sentences.zh: 即不充國用，不給邊需，猶當六年乃足。

translations.literal: Even if none went to state expenditure and none to frontier needs, it would still take six years to fill that quota.
translations.idiomatic: Even if every penny were devoted to the jewels alone—not a coin for the treasury or the frontier—it would still take six years to meet that quota.

sentences.zh: 必待取盈而後舉大禮，幾無時矣。」

translations.literal: If one must wait until the quota is filled before holding the great rite, there will practically be no time at all."
translations.idiomatic: To defer the great ceremony until the quota is filled is to defer it forever."

sentences.zh: 已，又言：「太祖、成祖、仁宗，即位初，即建儲貳。

translations.literal: Having finished, he also said: "Taizu, Chengzu, and Renzong, at the beginning of their reigns, immediately established the heir secondary.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Taizu, Chengzu, and Renzong all designated heirs soon after taking the throne.

sentences.zh: 宣宗、英宗冊為皇太子時，止二歲，憲宗、孝宗止六歲，陛下亦以六歲。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong and Yingzong were invested as crown princes they were only two years old; Xianzong and Xiaozong only six—and Your Majesty was also six.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong and Yingzong were invested at two; Xianzong and Xiaozong at six—Your Majesty yourself was six.

sentences.zh: 未聞年十九而不冊立者。」

translations.literal: One has never heard of someone nineteen years old who was not yet invested."
translations.idiomatic: No heir has ever reached nineteen without investiture."

sentences.zh: 國祚攝尚書近二年，爭國本至數十疏，儲位卒定。

translations.literal: Guozuo acting as minister for nearly two years submitted dozens of memorials disputing the foundation of the state, and the heirship was finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly two years as acting minister, Guozuo fought the succession issue in dozens of memorials until the heir was finally established.

sentences.zh: 陜西狄道山崩，其南湧小山五，國祚請修省。

translations.literal: At Didao in Shaanxi a mountain collapsed, and to its south five small hills welled up; Guozuo requested self-examination and reform.
translations.idiomatic: When a mountain collapsed at Didao in Shaanxi and five small peaks rose to its south, Guozuo urged the emperor to examine his conduct and amend policy.

sentences.zh: 社稷壇枯樹生煙，復陳安人心、收人望、通下情、清濫獄四事。

translations.literal: At the Altar of Soil and Grain a withered tree emitted smoke; he again set forth four matters—settling people's hearts, winning public esteem, opening channels to popular sentiment, and clearing wrongful imprisonments.
translations.idiomatic: When a dead tree at the Altar of Soil and Grain began to smoke, he again urged four reforms: reassuring the people, restoring public confidence, hearing grievances from below, and cleaning up abusive prisons.

sentences.zh: 雲南巡撫陳用賓進土物，國祚劾之。

translations.literal: The Yunnan grand coordinator Chen Yongbin presented local products; Guozuo impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yunnan grand coordinator Chen Yongbin sent local tribute goods to court, Guozuo impeached him.

sentences.zh: 尋轉左侍郎，改吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to left vice minister and moved to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left vice minister and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 御史湯兆京劾其縱酒逾檢，帝不問，國祚遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: The censor Tang Zhaojing impeached him for drinking unrestrainedly beyond propriety; the emperor did not inquire, and Guozuo thereupon pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Tang Zhaojing accused him of drunken excess, the emperor took no action, and Guozuo cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，以國祚嘗侍潛邸，特旨拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，入閣參機務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong acceded, because Guozuo had once served at the hidden residence, by special edict he was appointed minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the cabinet to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Guozuo—who had served him before his elevation—was specially appointed minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the cabinet to help govern.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年六月還朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianqi he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court in the sixth month of Tianqi 1 (1621).

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太保，進文淵閣。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and advanced to the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and moved to the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 國祚素行清慎，事持大體，稱長者。

translations.literal: Guozuo's conduct had always been pure and cautious; in affairs he held to the major principles and was called an elder statesman.
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo was known for integrity and restraint; he kept sight of larger principles and was respected as a senior figure of the court.

sentences.zh: 明年會試，故事，總裁止用內閣一人，是科用何宗彥及國祚，有譏其中旨特用者。

translations.literal: The next year at the metropolitan examination, by precedent the chief examiner used only one member of the Grand Secretariat; this session used He Zongyan and Guozuo together, and some ridiculed this as a special appointment by secret imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: At the next metropolitan examination, custom allowed only one grand secretary as chief examiner—but both He Zongyan and Guozuo were appointed, drawing whispers of a secret edict from the throne.

sentences.zh: 國祚既竣事，即求罷，優詔不允。

translations.literal: Once Guozuo had finished his duties, he immediately asked to be relieved; a gracious edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the examinations were over, Guozuo asked to step down; the emperor's gracious reply refused him.

sentences.zh: 都御史鄒元標侍經筵而躓，帝遣中使問狀。

translations.literal: When the censor-in-chief Zou Yuanbiao stumbled while attending the lecture sessions, the emperor sent a eunuch messenger to inquire after his condition.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Zou Yuanbiao stumbled during an imperial lecture, the emperor sent a eunuch to ask what had happened.

sentences.zh: 國祚進曰：「元標在先朝直言受杖，故步履猶艱。」

translations.literal: Guozuo stepped forward and said: "Yuanbiao, in the previous reign, spoke bluntly and was beaten with the rod, so his gait is still difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo replied: "Zou Yuanbiao was beaten for speaking out under the previous emperor—his gait has never fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 帝為之改容。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression on his account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression softened.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書王紀為魏忠賢所逐，國祚合疏救，復具私揭爭之。

translations.literal: When the minister of Justice Wang Ji was driven out by Wei Zhongxian, Guozuo joined memorials to save him and again submitted a private memorial to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Justice Wang Ji was hounded out by Wei Zhongxian, Guozuo signed collective memorials in his defense and filed a private remonstrance as well.

sentences.zh: 紀為禮部侍郎時，嘗以事忤國祚者也。

translations.literal: When Ji had been vice minister of Rites, he had once offended Guozuo over a matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji had once crossed Guozuo when he was vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三年，進少保、太子太保、戶部尚書，改武英殿。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to Junior Guardian, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and minister of Revenue, and moved to the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 3 (1623) he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, made minister of Revenue, and transferred to the Wuying Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十三疏乞休，詔加少傅兼太子太傅，乘傳歸。

translations.literal: After thirteen memorials begging retirement, an edict added Junior Mentor and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and he returned home by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: After thirteen petitions to retire, he was granted the titles of Junior Mentor and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and sent home by official courier.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Mentor and the posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Mentor with the posthumous name Wenge ("Cultured and Reverent").

sentences.zh: 從子大啟，文選郎中，終刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: His nephew Daqi, a director in the Bureau of Appointments, ended as left vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zhu Daqi, who had served as a director in the Bureau of Appointments, rose to left vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 朱國禎

translations.literal: Zhu Guozhen
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guozhen

sentences.zh: 同時朱國禎，字文寧，烏程人。

translations.literal: At the same period Zhu Guozhen, styled Wening, was a native of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: A contemporary, Zhu Guozhen—courtesy name Wening—was a native of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Wanli 17 (1589).

sentences.zh: 累官祭酒，謝病歸，久不出。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to chancellor of the Imperial Academy, pleaded illness and returned home, and for a long time did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chancellor of the Imperial Academy, retired citing illness, and stayed out of public life for many years.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，擢禮部右侍郎，未上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he was promoted to right vice minister of Rites but did not assume the post.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1 (1621) he was promoted to right vice minister of Rites but never reported to office.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，與顧秉謙、朱延禧、魏廣微並命。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he was appointed minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, together with Gu Bingqian, Zhu Yanxi, and Wei Guangwei in a single batch of appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianqi 3 (1623) he was appointed minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, along with Gu Bingqian, Zhu Yanxi, and Wei Guangwei in the same edict.

sentences.zh: 閣中已有葉向高、韓爌、何宗彥、朱國祚、史繼偕，又驟增四人，直房幾不容坐。

translations.literal: The cabinet already had Ye Xianggao, Han Kuang, He Zongyan, Zhu Guozuo, and Shi Jixie; with four more suddenly added, the duty room could scarcely hold seats for all.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat already held Ye Xianggao, Han Kuang, He Zongyan, Zhu Guozuo, and Shi Jixie; the sudden addition of four more left barely room to sit in the duty chamber.

sentences.zh: 六月，國禎還朝，秉謙、延禧以列名在後，謙居其次。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Guozhen returned to court; Bingqian and Yanxi, because their names were listed later, Bingqian ranked next after him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhen returned in the sixth month, Gu Bingqian and Zhu Yanxi—listed after him in seniority—ranked below him, with Gu Bingqian next in precedence.

sentences.zh: 改文淵閣大學士，累加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: He was changed to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and cumulatively promoted to Junior Guardian and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Wenyuan Pavilion and eventually rose to Junior Guardian and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢竊國柄，國禎佐向高，多所調護。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian usurped state power; Guozhen assisted Xianggao and in many matters mediated and protected.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian seized power, Guozhen worked alongside Ye Xianggao to mitigate and shield where he could.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，楊漣劾忠賢，廷臣多勸向高出疏，至有詬者。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year Yang Lian impeached Zhongxian; many court officials urged Xianggao to submit a memorial, and some even reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Tianqi 4 (1624), when Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, many urged Ye Xianggao to speak out—and some denounced him when he would not.

sentences.zh: 向高慍甚，國禎請容之。

translations.literal: Xianggao was greatly indignant; Guozhen asked that he be given forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao was furious; Guozhen begged the others to show him patience.

sentences.zh: 及向高密奏忤忠賢，決計去，謂國禎曰：「我去，蒲州更非其敵，公亦當早歸。」

translations.literal: When Xianggao's secret memorial offended Zhongxian and he resolved to leave, he said to Guozhen: "When I go, Puzhou will be even less his match—you too should return home early."
translations.idiomatic: When Ye Xianggao's confidential memorial provoked Wei Zhongxian and he decided to go, he told Guozhen: "Once I leave, Han Kuang will be no match for him—you should retire while you still can."

sentences.zh: 蒲州謂爌也。

translations.literal: Puzhou meant Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Puzhou" was Han Kuang.

sentences.zh: 向高罷，爌為首輔，爌罷，國禎為首輔。

translations.literal: Xianggao was dismissed; Kuang became chief minister; Kuang was dismissed; Guozhen became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao left office; Han Kuang became chief grand secretary; when Han Kuang fell, Guozhen took his place.

sentences.zh: 廣微與忠賢表裏為奸，視國禎蔑如。

translations.literal: Guangwei and Zhongxian worked together as inside and outside partners in villainy and regarded Guozhen as nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangwei and Wei Zhongxian worked hand in glove and treated Guozhen with utter contempt.

sentences.zh: 其冬為逆黨李蕃所劾，三疏引疾。

translations.literal: That winter he was impeached by Li Fan of the hostile faction and submitted three memorials pleading illness.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the hostile-faction censor Li Fan impeached him; Guozhen petitioned three times to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 忠賢謂其黨曰：「此老亦邪人，但不作惡，可令善去。」

translations.literal: Zhongxian said to his faction: "This old man is also a heterodox person, but he does no evil—let him be allowed to leave honorably."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian told his allies: "The old man is one of us in spirit, but he does no harm—let him take a graceful exit.

sentences.zh: 乃加少傅，賜銀幣，蔭子中書舍人，遣行人送歸，月廩、輿夫皆如制。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given Junior Mentor, granted silver and silk, his son was granted the privilege of a secretary in the Palace Secretariat, a courier was dispatched to escort him home, and monthly rations and sedan-chair bearers were all according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was granted the title of Junior Mentor, silver and silk, and a hereditary secretaryship for his son; an envoy escorted him home with full salary and sedan-chair bearers as regulation prescribed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chongzhen 5 (1632).

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Mentor and the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Mentor with the posthumous name Wensu ("Cultured and Stern").

sentences.zh: 何宗彥

translations.literal: He Zongyan
translations.idiomatic: He Zongyan

sentences.zh: 何宗彥，字君美。

translations.literal: He Zongyan, styled Junmei.
translations.idiomatic: He Zongyan, courtesy name Junmei.

sentences.zh: 其父由金谿客隨州，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father, traveling from Jinxi as a sojourner, settled in Suizhou and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father had left Jinxi to live in Suizhou as a guest and settled there permanently.

sentences.zh: 宗彥舉萬曆二十三年進士。

translations.literal: Zongyan passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan took his jinshi degree in Wanli 23 (1595).

sentences.zh: 累官詹事。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四十二年遷禮部右侍郎，署部事。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was transferred to right vice minister of Rites and acted over the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 42 (1614) he became right vice minister of Rites and took charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 福王之國河南，請求無已。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu went to his fief in Henan, his demands were ceaseless.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu took up residence in Henan, his demands never ceased.

sentences.zh: 宗彥上疏，言可慮者有六，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Zongyan submitted a memorial saying there were six matters worthy of concern; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan memorialized with six points of concern; the emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 又屢疏請東宮講學，皇孫就傅，及瑞、惠、桂三王婚禮。

translations.literal: He again repeatedly memorialized requesting lectures in the Eastern Palace, tutors for the imperial grandson, and the wedding rites for the Princes Rui, Hui, and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly urged imperial lectures for the Eastern Palace, tutors for the imperial grandson, and wedding ceremonies for the Princes Rui, Hui, and Gui.

sentences.zh: 太子生母王貴妃薨，不置守墳內官，又不置墳戶贍地，宗彥力爭之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince's birth mother, Imperial Noble Consort Wang, died, no inner eunuchs were assigned to guard the tomb and no tomb households or maintenance lands were established; Zongyan vigorously disputed this.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Wang, the crown prince's mother, died, the court assigned no eunuchs to watch her tomb and granted no maintenance households or lands—Zongyan fought bitterly against both omissions.

sentences.zh: 梃擊事起，宗彥因言：「天下疑陛下薄太子久。

translations.literal: When the club-attack affair arose, Zongyan thereupon said: "All under Heaven for a long time has suspected that Your Majesty slighted the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After the club-assault incident, Zongyan wrote: "For years the realm has suspected that Your Majesty holds the crown prince in low regard.

sentences.zh: 太子處積輕之勢，致慈慶宮門止守以耄年二內侍，中門則寂無一人。

translations.literal: The crown prince was in an accumulated condition of being looked down upon, such that at the gate of Ciqing Palace there were only two aged inner attendants on guard, and at the middle gate there was not a single person—utter silence.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has been left in a position of accumulating neglect: at the gate of Ciqing Palace only two aged eunuchs stand watch, and the inner gate stands entirely deserted.

sentences.zh: 乞亟下張差廷訊，凡青宮諸典禮，悉允臣部施行，宗社幸甚。」

translations.literal: I beg that Zhang Cha be immediately interrogated at court, and that all ceremonial matters of the Eastern Palace be entirely approved for execution by my ministry—great fortune for the altars of state and grain."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to have Zhang Cha interrogated at once and to authorize my ministry to carry out every ceremony owed the Eastern Palace—the altars of state and grain would be greatly served.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 尋轉左侍郎，署部如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to left vice minister and continued acting over the ministry as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left vice minister while continuing to run the ministry as before.

sentences.zh: 四十四年冬，隆德殿災，宗彥請通下情，修廢政，補曠官。

translations.literal: In the winter of the forty-fourth year the Longde Hall burned; Zongyan requested opening channels to popular sentiment, repairing abandoned policies, and filling vacant offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Longde Hall burned in the winter of Wanli 44 (1616), Zongyan called for hearing the people, restoring neglected reforms, and filling vacant posts.

sentences.zh: 明年，皇長孫年十三，未就傅，宗彥再疏力言。

translations.literal: The next year the imperial eldest grandson was thirteen years old and had not yet received tutors; Zongyan again memorialized, speaking forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the imperial grandson turned thirteen without tutors; Zongyan memorialized again, pressing the point urgently.

sentences.zh: 自是頻歲懇請，帝終不納。

translations.literal: From then on he earnestly petitioned year after year; the emperor in the end never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded year after year; the emperor never complied.

sentences.zh: 四十六年六月，京師地震。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the forty-sixth year the capital suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Wanli 46 (1618), Beijing was struck by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 上修省三事。

translations.literal: He submitted three matters of self-examination and reform.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three proposals for imperial self-examination and reform.

sentences.zh: 時帝不視朝已三十載，朝政積弛，庶官盡曠。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had not held court for thirty years; court governance had accumulated laxity and common offices were entirely vacant.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had avoided court audiences for thirty years; government had grown slack and ordinary posts stood empty.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，遼事益棘。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the next year the Liaodong situation grew increasingly critical.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn the Liaodong crisis grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 宗彥率僚屬上言：「自三路喪師，開原、鐵嶺相繼沒，沈陽孤危。

translations.literal: Zongyan led his subordinates in a memorial saying: "Since the three routes lost their armies, Kaiyuan and Tieling fell in succession, and Shenyang stands isolated and in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan and his staff memorialized: "Since our armies were destroyed on three fronts, Kaiyuan and Tieling have fallen in turn, and Shenyang stands alone and in peril.

sentences.zh: 請陛下臨朝，與臣等面籌兵食大計。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to come to court and face-to-face with us plan the great strategy for troops and provisions."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to hold court and meet with us face to face to decide the strategy for troops and supplies.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不報。

translations.literal: The emperor also gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Again the emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 弟宗聖，由鄉舉歷官工部主事。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zongsheng, through the provincial examination, rose through offices to chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zong Sheng, a provincial degree holder, rose to chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 以附魏忠賢，驟加本部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Because he attached himself to Wei Zhongxian, he was suddenly promoted to right vice minister of his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: By attaching himself to Wei Zhongxian, he was abruptly promoted to right vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，削籍，論配，名麗逆案。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, he was stricken from the registry, sentenced to penal exile, and his name was listed on the Treason Case.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Chongzhen reign he was stricken from the rolls, sentenced to penal exile, and his name was entered on the Treason Case.

sentences.zh: 孫如游

translations.literal: Sun Ruyou
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ruyou

sentences.zh: 孫如遊，字景文，餘姚人，都御史燧曾孫也。

translations.literal: Sun Ruyou, styled Jingwen, was a native of Yuyao and the great-grandson of Censor-in-Chief Sun Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ruyou, courtesy name Jingwen, was from Yuyao and a great-grandson of Censor-in-Chief Sun Sui.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Wanli 23 (1595).

sentences.zh: 累官禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to right vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to right vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十七年冬，左侍郎何宗彥去位，署印無人，大學士方從哲屢以如遊請。

translations.literal: In the winter of the forty-seventh year, left vice minister He Zongyan left his post; with no one to hold the acting seal, Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe repeatedly requested Ruyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 47 (1619), left vice minister He Zongyan vacated his post. With no one left to hold the ministry seal, Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe repeatedly recommended Ruyou.

sentences.zh: 明年三月始得命。

translations.literal: Not until the third month of the following year did he receive the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment did not come until the third month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 部事叢積，如遊決遣無滯。

translations.literal: Ministry affairs had piled up in heaps; Ruyou decided and dispatched them without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry business had piled up in heaps; Ruyou cleared the backlog without a hitch.

sentences.zh: 時白蓮、無為諸邪教橫行，宗彥嘗疏請嚴禁，如遊復申其說。

translations.literal: At the time the White Lotus, Wuwei, and other heterodox sects ran rampant; Zongyan had once memorialized requesting a strict ban, and Ruyou reiterated his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The White Lotus, Wuwei, and other heterodox sects were running rampant. Zongyan had once memorialized for a strict ban, and Ruyou now pressed the same case.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝疾大漸，偕諸大臣受顧命。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the emperor's illness grew grave; together with the chief ministers he received the deathbed charge.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor's illness turned critical, and Ruyou joined the chief ministers in receiving the deathbed charge.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，鄭貴妃懼禍，深結李選侍，為請封後。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Consort Zheng feared disaster, bonded deeply with Lady Li the concubine-attendant, and asked that she be ennobled as empress.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death, Consort Zheng, fearing retribution, cultivated a close tie with Lady Li the concubine-attendant and asked that she be made empress.

sentences.zh: 選侍喜，亦為請封太后以悅之。

translations.literal: The concubine-attendant was pleased and likewise asked that Consort Zheng be ennobled as empress dowager to delight her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was delighted and, to please her in return, asked that Consort Zheng be made empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 楊漣語如遊曰：「皇長子非選侍所愛。

translations.literal: Yang Lian said to Ruyou: "The eldest imperial son is not loved by the concubine-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lian told Ruyou: "The crown prince is not loved by Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 選侍後，嫡矣，他日將若何？

translations.literal: If the concubine-attendant becomes empress, she will be the legitimate wife—what then in days to come?
translations.idiomatic: If she becomes empress, she will be the legitimate consort—what then will become of the heir?

sentences.zh: 亟白執政，用遺詔舉冊立。

translations.literal: Quickly inform the chief ministers and use the deathbed edict to propose investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Inform the chief ministers at once and invoke the deathbed edict to press for investiture.

sentences.zh: 登極三日，公即援詔以請。」

translations.literal: Three days after enthronement, Your Excellency should cite the edict to request it."
translations.idiomatic: Three days after the new emperor takes the throne, cite the edict and submit the request yourself."

sentences.zh: 如遊然之。

translations.literal: Ruyou agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyou agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月朔，光宗即位。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month the Guangzong Emperor succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 三日，如遊請建東宮，帝納之。

translations.literal: On the third day Ruyou requested the establishment of the Eastern Palace; the emperor accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day Ruyou requested that the Eastern Palace be established; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄遵遺旨諭閣臣，封貴妃為皇太后。

translations.literal: Soon, following the deathbed will, he instructed the grand secretaries to ennoble Consort Zheng as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, acting on the late emperor's will, he instructed the grand secretaries to ennoble Consort Zheng as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 如遊奏曰：「考累朝典禮，以配而後者，乃敵體之經；

translations.literal: Ruyou memorialized, saying: "Examining the ritual precedents of successive reigns, an empress who was the principal consort is the constant rule of equal standing;
translations.idiomatic: Ruyou memorialized: "Reviewing the ritual precedents of successive reigns, an empress who was the principal consort embodies the constant rule of equal standing;

sentences.zh: 以妃而後者，則從子之義。

translations.literal: an empress who was a consort follows the principle of standing as a mother to the son.
translations.idiomatic: an empress who was merely a consort follows the principle of standing in relation to the son.

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，豈無抱衾之愛，而終引去席之嫌，此禮所不載也。

translations.literal: Since the founding ancestors, were there not affections of shared bedding, yet in the end the suspicion of usurping the mat was invoked and withdrawn—this the rites do not record.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, emperors have known intimate favor, yet in the end the suspicion of usurping the empress's place has always been invoked—and such a title the rites do not provide for.

sentences.zh: 先帝念貴妃勞，不在無名之位號；

translations.literal: The late emperor, mindful of the consort's labors, did not intend a title without proper standing;
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, mindful of the consort's service, did not mean to grant a title without proper standing;

sentences.zh: 陛下體先帝誌，亦不在非分之尊崇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, embodying the late emperor's intent, likewise should not grant honor beyond what is due.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, honoring the late emperor's intent, should likewise not bestow honor beyond what is due.

sentences.zh: 若義所不可，則遵命非孝，遵禮為孝。

translations.literal: If righteousness forbids it, then to follow the command is not filial; to follow the rites is filial.
translations.idiomatic: Where righteousness forbids it, obedience to the command is not filial piety—obedience to ritual is.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢曲徇，自蹈不忠之罪。」

translations.literal: Your servant dares not bend to please and thereby fall into the crime of disloyalty."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not bend to please and thereby invite the charge of disloyalty."

sentences.zh: 疏入，未報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 如遊尋進本部尚書。

translations.literal: Ruyou was soon promoted to minister of his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyou was soon promoted to minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝既命建東宮，又言皇長子體質清弱，稍緩冊立期。

translations.literal: The emperor, having ordered the establishment of the Eastern Palace, also said the eldest imperial son's constitution was delicate and weak and wished to delay the date of investiture somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Having ordered the Eastern Palace established, the emperor also said the crown prince's constitution was frail and wished to delay the investiture somewhat.

sentences.zh: 如遊力持不可。

translations.literal: Ruyou forcefully maintained that this would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyou firmly objected.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，命封選侍為皇貴妃。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day he ordered Lady Li the concubine-attendant ennobled as imperial noble consort.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third day he ordered Lady Li ennobled as imperial noble consort.

sentences.zh: 期已定矣，越三日，帝又趨之。

translations.literal: The date had already been fixed; three days later the emperor again pressed to hurry it.
translations.idiomatic: The date had been set, but three days later the emperor pressed again to hurry matters along.

sentences.zh: 如遊奏曰：「先奉諭上孝端皇后、孝靖皇太后尊諡，又封郭元妃、王才人為皇后，禮皆未竣，貴妃之封宜在後。

translations.literal: Ruyou memorialized, saying: "We were first commanded to confer posthumous honorific titles upon Empress Xiaoduan and Empress Dowager Xiaojing, and also to ennoble Consort Guo Yuan and Lady Wang the Talented Lady as empresses—these rites are not yet complete, so the consort's ennoblement should come afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyou memorialized: "We were first commanded to confer posthumous titles on Empress Xiaoduan and Empress Dowager Xiaojing, and also to ennoble Consort Guo Yuan and Lady Wang the Talented Lady as empresses—none of these rites is yet complete, so the noble consort's ennoblement should wait.

sentences.zh: 既聖諭諄切，且有保護聖儲功，即如先所定期，亦無不可。」

translations.literal: Since the sacred instruction is earnest, and she moreover has merit in protecting the sacred heir, to proceed on the previously fixed date would also be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's instruction is earnest, and she has merit in protecting the heir, proceeding on the date already fixed would also be acceptable."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 選侍以貴妃為未足，必欲得皇后。

translations.literal: The concubine-attendant regarded imperial noble consort as insufficient and insisted on obtaining the title of empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li found imperial noble consort insufficient and insisted on becoming empress.

sentences.zh: 二十九日，再召廷臣，選侍迫皇長子言之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day the emperor again summoned the court ministers; the concubine-attendant forced the eldest imperial son to speak on her behalf.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day the emperor again summoned the court ministers, and Lady Li forced the crown prince to speak for her.

sentences.zh: 如遊曰：「上欲封選侍為皇貴妃，當即具儀進。」

translations.literal: Ruyou said: "Your Majesty wishes to ennoble the concubine-attendant as imperial noble consort; the rites should be prepared and submitted at once."
translations.idiomatic: Ruyou said: "If Your Majesty wishes to ennoble Lady Li as imperial noble consort, the rites should be prepared and submitted at once."

sentences.zh: 帝漫應曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: The emperor answered casually: "Very well."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered offhandedly: "Very well."

sentences.zh: 選侍聞，大不悅。

translations.literal: When the concubine-attendant heard this, she was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li heard this and was furious.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝崩，朝事大變。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor died, and court affairs changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor died, and court affairs were transformed overnight.

sentences.zh: 如遊請改冊封期，報可。

translations.literal: Ruyou requested that the date of investiture and ennoblement be changed; approval was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyou asked that the ennoblement date be changed; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 熹宗為皇孫時，未就傅。

translations.literal: When Xizong was imperial grandson, he had not yet received tutors.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Xizong Emperor was still imperial grandson, he had not yet been given tutors.

sentences.zh: 即位七日，如遊即請開講筵，亦報可。

translations.literal: Seven days after enthronement Ruyou at once requested that the lecture hall be opened; approval was likewise returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days after his enthronement, Ruyou at once requested that the heir's lecture hall be opened; that too was approved.

sentences.zh: 孫嘉績

translations.literal: Sun Jiaji
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiaji

sentences.zh: 孫嘉績，字碩膚。

translations.literal: Sun Jiaji, styled Shuofu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiaji, courtesy name Shuofu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Chongzhen 10 (1637).

sentences.zh: 授南京工部主事，召改兵部。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, then summoned and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, then recalled and transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 大清兵薄都城，按營不動，眾莫測。

translations.literal: Great Qing troops pressed close to the capital and encamped without moving; no one could fathom their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Qing troops pressed close to the capital and encamped without moving; no one could fathom their intent.

sentences.zh: 嘉績曰：「此待後至者，即舉眾南下爾。」

translations.literal: Jiaji said: "This is waiting for those arriving later; then the whole force will march south, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Jiaji said: "They are waiting for reinforcements—then the whole army will march south."

sentences.zh: 越三日，蒙古兵數萬果從青山口入，即日南下。

translations.literal: Three days later tens of thousands of Mongol troops indeed entered through Qingshan Pass and the same day marched south.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later tens of thousands of Mongol troops entered through Qingshan Pass and marched south the same day.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書楊嗣昌以嘉績知兵，調為職方員外郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister Yang Sichang, judging that Jiaji understood military affairs, transferred him to be an assistant director in the Bureau of Operations.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yang Sichang, judging that Jiaji understood military affairs, transferred him to assistant director in the Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 進郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 督師中官高起潛譖之，會有發其納賄事，遂下獄。

translations.literal: The supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian slandered him; it happened that his taking bribes was exposed, and he was thereupon imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian slandered him; when his taking bribes was exposed, he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 已，黃道周亦下獄。

translations.literal: Before long Huang Daozhou was also imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huang Daozhou was imprisoned as well.

sentences.zh: 嘉績躬親飲食湯藥，力調護之，因從受《易》。

translations.literal: Jiaji personally attended to his food, drink, and medicines, exerting himself to nurse him, and in the process received instruction in the Changes from him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaji personally tended his food, drink, and medicines, nursing him with devoted care, and in the process studied the Book of Changes under his tutelage.

sentences.zh: 會諸生塗仲吉疏救道周，帝益怒，移獄錦衣嚴訊。

translations.literal: It happened that the student Tu Zhongji memorialized to save Daozhou; the emperor grew still angrier and transferred the case to the Brocade Guard for strict interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When the student Tu Zhongji memorialized to save Daozhou, the emperor grew still angrier and transferred the case to the Brocade Guard for harsh interrogation.

sentences.zh: 諸生與道周往來者多詭詞自脫，獨嘉績無所隱。

translations.literal: Many students who had dealings with Daozhou used evasive words to extricate themselves; Jiaji alone concealed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Many students who had associated with Daozhou used evasive words to save themselves; Jiaji alone held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 擬雜犯死罪，繼擬煙瘴充軍，皆不允。

translations.literal: They proposed a mixed capital offense carrying death; then proposed exile to malarial frontier service—neither was approved.
translations.idiomatic: A mixed capital offense carrying death was proposed, then exile to the malarial frontier—neither was approved.

sentences.zh: 保定總督張福臻陛見，薦嘉績才，請用為參謀，不聽。

translations.literal: Baoding governor-general Zhang Fuzhen had an audience at court, recommended Jiaji's talent, and requested that he be employed as a staff officer; the request was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding governor-general Zhang Fuzhen had an audience at court, praised Jiaji's talent, and asked that he be employed as a staff officer; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 徐石麒為刑部尚書，具爰書奏，乃釋之。

translations.literal: Xu Shiqin, as minister of Justice, prepared the case report and memorialized; only then was Jiaji released.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiqin, as minister of Justice, prepared the case report and memorialized; only then was Jiaji released.

sentences.zh: 福王時，起九江兵備僉事，未赴。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu he was appointed military intendant at Jiujiang but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was appointed military intendant at Jiujiang but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國紹興，擢右僉都御史，累進東閣大學士。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu acted as regent at Shaoxing, Jiaji was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and in succession advanced to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu acted as regent at Shaoxing, Jiaji was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and eventually rose to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 王航海，嘉績從至舟山。

translations.literal: When the prince put to sea, Jiaji followed him as far as Zhoushan.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took to the sea, Jiaji followed him to Zhoushan.

sentences.zh: 其年遘疾卒。

translations.literal: That same year he met with illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：熹宗初，葉向高以宿望召起，海內正人倚以為重，卒不能有所匡救。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the beginning of Xizong's reign, Ye Xianggao was summoned back on account of long-standing repute; upright men throughout the realm relied on him as a weighty figure, yet in the end he could not rescue the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Early in the Xizong reign, Ye Xianggao was recalled for his long-standing repute, and upright men throughout the realm looked to him as a pillar of the court—yet in the end he could not set things right.

sentences.zh: 蓋政柄內移，非一日之積，勢固無如何也。

translations.literal: For political power had shifted inward—not the accumulation of a single day—and the situation by its nature could not be helped.
translations.idiomatic: Political power had been shifting inward for years, not days—and against such a tide there was little to be done.

sentences.zh: 劉一燝、韓爌諸人，雖居端揆之地，而宵小比肩，權珰掣肘，紛撓杌隉，幾不自全。

translations.literal: Liu Yijing, Han Kuang, and the like, though they occupied the place of chief ministers, had petty men standing shoulder to shoulder with them, powerful eunuchs holding them back, turmoil and instability in confusion—they could scarcely preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing, Han Kuang, and their peers held the chief minister's seat, yet petty men crowded in beside them, powerful eunuchs held them in check, and turmoil left them barely able to preserve themselves.

sentences.zh: 朱國祚、何宗彥絀於黨人，孫如遊又皆以中旨特用，為外廷所詬。

translations.literal: Zhu Guozuo and He Zongyan were displaced by factional men; Sun Ruyou likewise was specially appointed by secret imperial edict—all were reviled by the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guozuo and He Zongyan were pushed aside by factional rivals; Sun Ruyou too was specially appointed by secret edict—all were reviled by the outer court.

sentences.zh: 於是而知明良相遭，誠千載之一遇也夫！

translations.literal: From this one knows that the meeting of a wise ruler and able ministers is truly an encounter once in a thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that the meeting of a wise ruler and able ministers is truly an encounter once in a thousand years!
